platform_notes: Korona POS is KORONA POS by COMBASE USA: a POS client that runs on Windows 10 or later (Java 17) and is configured from the KORONA Studio cloud back office; its manual documents PAX, Dejavoo, Genius and BlockChyp card terminals connected over the network. POS on iPhone is the Union POS app; Union's public help centre is written for Union iPad terminals with MagTek eDynamo/iDynamo card readers and a Manager Portal, and has no iPhone or Tap to Pay troubleshooting articles, so Union entries describe the same app on iPad hardware.

entries.title: Terminal will not power on or charge: check the power cables
steps: Make sure the charging cable is firmly plugged into the terminal.
Make sure the other end is firmly plugged into an outlet or surge protector.
Check that the outlet or surge protector has power; if the outlet is dead, check the circuit breaker.
Plug the terminal into an outlet you know works.
Swap the charging cable for one you know works.
entries.quote: Replace the terminal's charging cable with a known working cable.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Terminal still will not charge: test it apart from the card reader
steps: Unplug the card reader from the terminal and, if it has a case, take the reader out of its case.
Charge the terminal and the card reader separately, each on its own cable, for about 20 minutes.
Reconnect the two charged devices.
If the reader is an iDynamo6, turn the terminal off and on again after reconnecting.
If the terminal will not charge on its own, its charging port may need to be looked at in an Apple store.
If it still does not charge, stop and contact Support.
entries.quote: Charge both terminal and card reader with their individual charging cables, for approximately 20 minutes.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Where to get a replacement charging cable
steps: Order parts directly at parts.getunion.com, or follow Union's Order Replacement Hardware process.
entries.quote: If new charging cables are needed, refer to Order Replacement Hardware or order parts directly at parts.getunion.com.

entries.title: Card reader not working: check the indicator light first
steps: Look at the indicator light on the card reader.
If it is green (solid or blinking), carry on with the re-pairing steps for your reader model.
If it is any other colour, or the light is out, stop and contact Support.
entries.quote: If the color is anything else: Stop troubleshooting and contact Support.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Re-pair an eDynamo card reader (Bluetooth)
steps: On the POS terminal, close the Union POS app and open iPad Settings.
Select Bluetooth and write down the reader's serial number as shown there (eDynamo-######).
Scroll down the left menu and select Union.
Check that Card Reader Model (iPad only) is set to eDynamo.
Check that the switch next to Enable Card Reader Pairing (eDynamo) is on and green.
Hold the small button on the left side of the eDynamo until the light flashes blue.
Close Settings and reopen the Union POS app; a popup appears.
Pick the reader by the serial number you wrote down.
When asked, swipe a test card to finish pairing. A 'Pairing was successful' message should show.
If pairing does not succeed, stop and contact Support.
entries.quote: Hold down the small button on the left hand side of eDynamo until light flashes blue to enable pairing.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Reset the connection to an iDynamo card reader
steps: Close the Union POS app on the terminal.
Open iPad Settings, scroll down the left menu and select Union.
Check that Card Reader Model is set to iDynamo.
Select General, scroll down and select Shut Down.
With the iPad off, unplug its power source from the back of the iPad or from the outlet.
Wait for the iPad to shut down completely.
Plug the power back in; the iPad should turn on by itself.
entries.quote: With the iPad powered off, unplug its power source from either the back of the iPad or the power outlet.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Cash drawer will not open: fix the receipt printer first
steps: The cash drawer is connected to the terminal through the receipt printer.
If the receipt printer is not working either, fix the printer first; that usually fixes the drawer.
Check that the cash drawer cable is firmly plugged into its port on the receipt printer.
entries.quote: A cash drawer is linked to the POS terminal through the connected receipt printer.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Cash drawer will not open: check whether it is locked
steps: Find the key that came with the drawer.
Put the key in and turn it counterclockwise to open the drawer.
If the key turns but the drawer does not open, the drawer is probably broken; order a new one from parts.getunion.com.
If the key is lost, a replacement can be bought at parts.getunion.com; if it is not listed there, contact Support.
entries.quote: Insert the key into the drawer and turn counterclockwise to open.

entries.title: Cash drawer opens with the key but not from the POS
steps: Run a test print from the printer the drawer is connected to.
If the printer works and the drawer opens with the key, the cord between printer and drawer is faulty.
Order a replacement from parts.getunion.com.
entries.quote: If the printer functions correctly, and the cash drawer opens with the key, the APG cord between the printer and cash drawer is faulty.

entries.title: Order replacement Union hardware
steps: Order common hardware items online at parts.getunion.com; search by item name or picture.
Online orders take about 48 hours to process, depending on stock.
Orders can also be placed through the Support team; those take 3 to 7 business days, depending on stock.
For a new terminal, contact Support.
entries.quote: Processing time for online orders: 48 hours, dependent on inventory availability.

entries.title: Get an update on a Union hardware order
steps: Reply to the order confirmation email and ask for an update, or contact Support.
entries.quote: Reply back to your order confirmation email and request an update; or

entries.title: A hardware item shows as Sold Out
steps: The online ordering page shows current stock, so Sold Out means Union is out of that item.
Contact Support to ask when it will be back in stock.
If an item already bought becomes backordered, Union will contact you with an availability date.
entries.quote: Reach out to Support to inquire when an item will be back in stock.

entries.title: Kitchen Display System (KDS) is not showing orders: remove other Wi-Fi networks
steps: Make sure at least one order for the KDS is open, or create a test order.
On the KDS terminal, close the KDS app and open iPad Settings.
Select WiFi, then Edit at the top right to see the saved networks.
If any non-Union networks are listed, select the red minus icon and Delete for each one.
Reopen the KDS app; orders should show again.
entries.quote: If the KDS is not displaying orders properly, the issue is often due to interference from other WiFi networks.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: KDS still not showing orders: check the POS terminals that send to it
steps: Close the KDS app on the KDS terminal.
On every POS terminal that prints to that KDS, close the Union POS app and open iPad Settings.
On each one, select WiFi, then Edit, and delete any non-Union networks.
When all terminals are checked, reopen the KDS app on the KDS terminal.
entries.quote: Once all connected terminals have been checked, reopen the KDS app on the KDS terminal.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: KDS still not showing orders: check the terminal is set to send to that KDS
steps: On a POS terminal that prints to the KDS, go to the Log In screen and note the Register ID in the bottom-right corner.
On another device, sign in to the Manager Portal.
Select Settings, then Hardware Setup, then Registers.
Select the terminal with that Register ID.
Check that the right KDS is selected in the KDS dropdown.
If it is already correct, stop and contact Support.
If it is wrong or empty, add the KDS, create a test order and check it appears on the KDS.
If the test order does not appear, stop and contact Support.
entries.quote: On the terminal's properties page, confirm that the KDS you are troubleshooting is selected from the KDS dropdown menu.

entries.title: Terminal seems offline: check it is not set to Offline Mode
steps: Log in to the Union POS app with Manager or Admin credentials.
Select the menu (three lines) at the upper left.
Select Turn Online/Offline Mode.
If Set to Online Mode is switched off, the terminal is in Offline Mode; switch it on to connect.
entries.quote: If the option "Set to Online Mode" is untoggled, this means you are in Offline Mode. Toggle it on to connect.

entries.title: Network trouble: power cycle the printers and read their test prints
steps: Unplug all printers from their power outlets.
Plug them back in.
Wait up to 5 minutes for each printer to print its test print.
Check that the IP addresses printed all begin with the same two numbers.
Keep the test prints until the connection is back, in case Support asks for them.
If a printer prints something odd or nothing at all, that printer needs its own troubleshooting.
entries.quote: Gather the test prints and ensure the IPs printed begin with the same two numbers.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Terminal keeps dropping: remove non-Union Wi-Fi networks
steps: Close the Union POS app and open iPad Settings.
Select WiFi, then Edit at the top right.
Find your Union network; most are named in a UNIONXX format.
Select the Info button (circled i) and write down the Wi-Fi IP address, in case Support needs it.
Delete every non-Union network using the red minus icon.
If no Union network is listed at all, stop and contact Support.
entries.quote: Most Union WiFi networks are named in a "UNIONXX" format.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Check whether the internet itself is down
steps: Open Safari on the terminal and try to load any website.
If it loads, the internet connection is working.
If nothing loads, find your internet modem (and router, if you have one).
Unplug their power cords for one minute and plug them back in.
Try loading a website again.
If it still will not load, call your internet service provider.
entries.quote: Unplug hardware power cords for one minute and plug back in.

entries.title: Internet is out: what the Union POS does offline
steps: The system is designed to keep running offline.
Do not run the End Of Day report or staff tipping until you are back online.
All transaction information is saved and reports run once you are online again.
Contact Support if you need help after reconnecting.
entries.quote: Hold off on running an End Of Day report or staff tipping until back online.

entries.title: Back online after an outage: check every terminal
steps: On each terminal, run a print test to confirm it is on the network.
Open Safari and load any website to confirm the internet is working.
If a terminal is still offline or will not print, follow the network troubleshooting steps.
entries.quote: Run a print test to ensure network connectivity.

entries.title: Back online after an outage: finish the previous day and run End of Day
steps: Sign in to the Union POS app with a PIN that has manager permissions.
On the All Checks screen choose All in the Employee dropdown and make sure no tabs are still open.
Choose All in the Status dropdown and check out any closed tabs that are still coloured (not checked out).
Make sure all staff tips have been entered.
From the menu (three lines), select Manage Employees and clock out anyone still clocked in.
From the menu, select Close Walked Checks, select all, then Close Selected Checks.
Run End of Day from the menu.
The previous day's data is then sent to the Manager Portal and the system is clear for a new service.
entries.quote: Verify that all tasks from the previous business day have been completed and run the End of Day task.

entries.title: Tabs with declined cards go into Recovery Mode
steps: Tabs whose cards declined are put into Recovery Mode by the system automatically.
Walked checks are closed from the menu (three lines) under Close Walked Checks.
entries.quote: Remember that tabs with declined cards will automatically go into Recovery Mode by the system.

entries.title: Close walked checks
steps: Select the menu (three lines) at the upper left.
Select Close Walked Checks.
Select all, then Close Selected Checks.
entries.quote: Select all, then Close Selected Checks.

entries.title: Clock out employees who are still clocked in
steps: Select the menu (three lines) at the upper left.
Select Manage Employees.
Clock out any active employees.
entries.quote: Clock out any active employees.

entries.title: Release an iPad that used to be a Union terminal from Union management (MDM)
steps: Unlock the iPad and open Settings, then General, then About.
Write down the serial number (one for each iPad to be released).
Email support@getunion.com with your name, your contact details, the venue name and each serial number.
Union replies within 48 hours; the release is typically completed in two to three business days.
entries.quote: Email support@getunion.com with all of the following:

entries.title: Add a new terminal to a Union POS setup
steps: Decide the terminal size: 12 inch, 10 inch, or 7.9 inch handheld.
Decide how it is mounted: counter stand, wall-mounted, or handheld with strap.
Choose a name that fits your other terminals (for example Reg 5, Bar) and avoid special characters.
Have the delivery address ready.
Contact Union Support at support@getunion.com or by phone with that information, your contact details, your venue, and any extra hardware such as cash drawers or printers.
entries.quote: Contact Support at support@getunion.com or via phone.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Printing is slow: remove other Wi-Fi networks from the terminal
steps: On each terminal that prints slowly, close the Union POS app.
Open iPad Settings, select WiFi, then Edit at the top right.
Delete any non-Union networks using the red minus icon.
entries.quote: At each POS terminal that has demonstrated slowed printing, check for bad WiFi connections.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Printing is slow: run an internet speed test
steps: Close the Union POS app and open Safari.
Type 'speed test' in the address bar and select Run Speed Test when the results load.
If the speed is under 15 Mbps, stop and call Support.
If it is 15 Mbps or more, go on to check the printer's cable.
entries.quote: If speeds are less than 15 Mbps: Stop troubleshooting and call Support.

entries.title: Printing is slow: check the printer Ethernet cable
steps: Find the Ethernet cable plugged into the printer and look for bends, breaks or frays.
Run a test print.
If printing is still slow, stop and contact Support.
entries.quote: Identify the ethernet cable connected to the printer and search for bends, breaks, or frays in the cable.

entries.title: Open a tab
steps: In the Union POS app, switch the filter at the top of the screen to Tabs view.
Select the blue New Tab button.
Add items to the tab.
entries.quote: Select the blue "New Tab" button.

entries.title: Assign a table to an employee
steps: Switch the filter at the top of the screen to Tables view.
Set the Mode filter to Assign.
Select the table or tables.
On the right, select the employee's name.
entries.quote: On the right, select the employee's name to assign the Table(s).

entries.title: Unassign a table from an employee
steps: Switch to Tables view and set the Mode filter to Assign.
Select the table or tables to remove the employee from.
On the right, select the employee's name to unassign them.
To unassign all of an employee's tables, long press the employee's name and select Unassign All Tables.
entries.quote: To unassign ALL tables from an employee, long press on the employee's name on the right, and select "Unassign All Tables".

entries.title: Open a To-Go order
steps: Switch the filter at the top of the screen to To-Go view.
Select the green New To-Go button.
Fill in what applies: customer name, pick up date and time, phone number, address.
Add items to the order.
entries.quote: Select the green "New To-Go" button.

entries.title: Take payment and close a check
steps: Select the tab, table or To-Go to show the check.
Select Pay at the bottom of the check screen.
Select the payment type and process the payment.
When the payment has gone through, the check shows a Balance Owed of $0.
Select Close at the bottom of the check screen.
A Fast Payment option closes the check automatically once payment is applied.
entries.quote: Once the Payment has processed, the Check will show a Balance Owed of $0.

entries.title: Reopen a closed check
steps: Switch the filter at the top of the screen to All Checks view.
Set the Status filter to Closed.
Set the Employee filter to whoever closed the check, or All Employees if unknown.
Select the closed check.
Select Reopen at the bottom of the check screen.
entries.quote: Select the "Reopen" button at the bottom of the Check screen.

entries.title: The Reopen button is missing on a closed check
steps: The logged-in employee does not have the POS permission to reopen a check.
A manager has to reopen the check.
entries.quote: If the "Reopen" button is missing, the employee who is logged in to the POS does not have the POS permission to reopen a check

entries.title: Discounts, voids and comps need manager approval on the terminal
steps: An employee can add an adjustment to a tab (discount, void, comp, tax-exempt, spill, gratuity, service charge, pricing event price).
A manager must approve it on the Union POS terminal before it applies.
A POS permission for each adjustment type in the Manager Portal lets a job role skip manager approval.
entries.quote: the adjustment must be approved on the Union POS terminal by a Manager in order to apply

entries.title: Void, comp and spill: which one to use
steps: Void removes the price of an item when no product was used or wasted.
Comp removes the price of an item when product was used or wasted.
Spill removes the price of an item that was spilled in the venue.
entries.quote: A void is used when NO product was used/wasted.

entries.title: Tax Exempt adjustment needs a tax exempt ID
steps: Tax Exempt removes all tax from the check.
A tax exempt ID must be entered to add it.
entries.quote: A tax exempt ID must be entered to add the Tax Exempt adjustment.

entries.title: Card payment types on the Union payment screen: Dip, Swipe, Enter Card
steps: Dip: insert the card into the dip slot so the chip is read.
Swipe: slide the card along the slot on top of the reader so the magnetic strip is read.
Enter Card: type the card details into the POS terminal by hand.
entries.quote: Enter Card: Process a credit card transaction by manually entering the credit card information on the POS terminal
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Pay At Table: the customer completes the payment
steps: Select Pay At Table.
Turn the screen to the customer.
The customer dips, taps or swipes their card, or scans the QR code and pays on their phone.
entries.quote: Once this option is selected, the screen is to be turned to the customer to either dip, tap, or swipe their credit card or to scan the QR code and pay with their phone.

entries.title: Fast Cash, Fast Card, Fast House Account, Fast Gift Card
steps: Fast Cash applies the full payment in cash and closes the check.
Fast Card closes the check automatically once a dipped, swiped or tapped card payment goes through.
Fast House Account applies the full payment to a chosen House Account and closes the check.
Fast Gift Card closes the check once the gift card is swiped and the payment goes through.
entries.quote: Fast Card: Once a card is dipped/swiped/tapped and the payment processes successfully, the check automatically closes

entries.title: Cash payment opens the cash drawer
steps: Choosing Cash processes a cash payment.
If a cash drawer is attached to the terminal it opens automatically.
entries.quote: If a cash drawer is attached to the POS terminal, it will automatically open for use.

entries.title: Take a gift card payment
steps: Choose Gift Card and swipe the gift card along the slot on top of the reader.
entries.quote: Gift Card: Process a Payment by swiping a Gift Card along the slot on the top of the reader
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Service charge and gratuity adjustments
steps: SVC Charge adds a percentage or dollar amount to a check, set by the venue.
Gratuity adds an extra charge (tip) for the server or bartender, set by the venue.
entries.quote: Gratuity: Add an extra charge (tip) for the server/bartender, by the venue

entries.title: Change what a job role is allowed to do on the POS
steps: Permissions belong to job roles, not to individual employees.
Only someone whose job role has Modify Permissions can change them.
Log in to the Manager Portal.
Select the menu (three lines), then Labor, then POS Permissions.
Tick or untick the boxes under each job role.
Select Save.
entries.quote: Permissions are assigned to job roles. Individual employees cannot have permissions assigned or removed--but custom job roles can be created.

entries.title: "Permission Required" (red message)
steps: The employee's job role does not have the permission for that action (for example joining checks, transferring checks, or activating gift cards).
Have a manager do it, or have someone with Modify Permissions turn the permission on for that job role in the Manager Portal under Labor, POS Permissions.
entries.quote: If an employee attempts to join checks but does not have this permission, they will receive a red "Permission Required" error message.

entries.title: Cash or Fast Cash is missing from the payment screen
steps: The Take Cash Payments permission is turned off for that employee's job role.
Turn it on in the Manager Portal under Labor, POS Permissions.
entries.quote: If this is turned off, the tender types "Cash" and "Fash Cash" do not display on the Payment screen.

entries.title: Swipe, Dip, Fast Card or Pay at the Table is missing from the payment screen
steps: The Take Cards by Swipe, Dip and Tap permission is turned off for that employee's job role.
Turn it on in the Manager Portal under Labor, POS Permissions.
entries.quote: If this is turned off, the tender types "Swipe", "Dip", "Fash Card", and "Pay at the Table" do not display on the Payment screen.

entries.title: Enter Card (manual card entry) is missing from the payment screen
steps: The Take Cards by Manual Card Entry permission is turned off for that employee's job role.
Turn it on in the Manager Portal under Labor, POS Permissions.
entries.quote: If this is turned off, the tender type "Enter Card" does not display on the Payment screen.

entries.title: Gift Card is missing from the payment screen
steps: The Take Gift Card Payments permission is turned off for that employee's job role.
Turn it on in the Manager Portal under Labor, POS Permissions.
entries.quote: If this is turned off, the tender type "Gift Card" does not display on the Payment screen.

entries.title: House Accounts is missing from the payment screen or side menu
steps: Take House Account Payments controls the House Accounts tender on the payment screen.
Manage House Accounts controls the Manage House Accounts option in the side menu.
Turn on the one that is missing for the job role in the Manager Portal under Labor, POS Permissions.
entries.quote: If this is turned off, the menu option "Manage House Accounts" will not display in the side menu of the Union POS

entries.title: Who can run End of Day
steps: Running End-of-Day to batch out sales needs the Manage End-of-Day Activities permission.
entries.quote: Manage End-of-Day Activities: Allows run of End-of-Day procedures to batch out sales

entries.title: Transferring a check to another employee
steps: The employee needs the Transfer Checks permission.
The employee receiving the check must accept or reject it.
entries.quote: The receiving employee MUST accept or reject the transferred check.

entries.title: Reprinting a lost kitchen ticket
steps: Reprinting an order ticket needs the Reprint Station Tickets permission.
entries.quote: Reprint Station Tickets: Allows reprint of an order ticket

entries.title: Opening the cash drawer without a sale
steps: The employee's job role needs the Open Cash Drawer Off Sale permission.
entries.quote: Open Cash Drawer Off Sale: Allows ability to open the cash drawer without making a cash sale on a check

entries.title: Cash Sales and Venue Keeps do not show on an employee checkout
steps: The View Cash Sales permission is turned off for that job role.
Turn it on in the Manager Portal under Labor, POS Permissions if the employee should see them.
entries.quote: If this is turned off, both Cash Sales and Venue Keeps data will not display for the employee on Checkout nor in the POS Sales Reporting

entries.title: An employee cannot add items to another employee's tab or table
steps: The Access Tabs, Access Tables and Access To-Go Orders permissions only cover the employee's own.
Adding to other employees' tabs, tables or to-go orders needs Manage All Tabs, Manage All Tables or Manage All To-Go.
entries.quote: These 3 "Manage All" permissions allow the employee to add items to other employees' tabs, tables, and to-go orders.

entries.title: 86-ing an item (item countdown)
steps: Item availability is managed through item countdown, which needs the Manage Item Countdown permission.
entries.quote: Manage Item Countdown: Allows access to item countdown, for managing item availability and 86-ing items

entries.title: Set the screen an employee sees after logging in
steps: Have the employee log in to the Union POS app with their PIN.
Switch the home screen to the view wanted: All Tabs, All Tables, All To-go or All Checks.
Set any filters wanted.
The POS remembers the last home screen and filters the next time that user logs in.
entries.quote: The Union POS will remember the last selected home screen and filters when the user logs in next.

entries.title: A table does not show on an employee's checkout
steps: A table must be assigned to an employee to show on their checkout.
Assign it in Tables view with the Mode filter set to Assign.
entries.quote: A Table must be assigned to an employee to show on their checkout.

entries.title: Cannot find a check on the screen
steps: Check the filters at the top: Status (Open, Closed, All), Employee, and Sort (Name or Time).
The All Checks view has a View filter for Tables, Tabs or To-Go.
In Tables view the POS shows only one floor plan at a time; change the Area filter.
entries.quote: Status: Displays a subset of checks based on open or closed state

entries.title: Open the End of Day report
steps: Log in to the Manager Portal (your job role needs the Run Reports permission).
Select the menu (three lines), then Reports, then End of Day.
entries.quote: On the Reports submenu, select "End of Day".

entries.title: End of Day report: gross sales, net sales and deposit lines
steps: Gross Sales is total sales before discounts, comps, spills or voids.
Net Sales is total sales after those adjustments.
Deposit Summary is the total of all card and cash payments taken.
Paid Ins/Paid Outs can be negative because of paid outs.
entries.quote: Deposit Summary: Total amount of all payment forms taken (both card and cash)

entries.title: End of Day report: tip lines
steps: Paid Tips is the tip total collected by servers (reported card tips and cash tips).
Retained Tips is the tip total kept by the venue, for taxes or fees if applicable.
Net Tips & Grats is card and other tips and gratuities minus Card Fees on Card Tips & Grats.
entries.quote: Paid Tips: Total tip amounts collected by server (all reported credit card tips and cash tips)

entries.title: Rounding on Union reports
steps: If the venue uses rounding, it always rounds down, in the customer's favour.
entries.quote: If your venue uses rounding, the round will always be in favor of the customer (round down)

entries.title: Open an employee Checkouts report
steps: Log in to the Manager Portal (your job role needs the Run Reports permission).
Select the menu (three lines), then Reports, then Checkouts.
The report shows one employee's contribution to the End of Day numbers.
entries.quote: The Checkouts Report is a way to view an individual employee's contribution toward End of Day numbers.

entries.title: Checkout report: Venue Keeps is negative
steps: Venue Keeps is the amount of cash kept by the venue.
It can be negative when more sales and tips came from cards than from cash.
entries.quote: This can be a negative amount if more sales and tips come from card sales than cash sales.

entries.title: Reconcile card transactions against deposits with the Transaction Report
steps: Log in to the Manager Portal, select the menu (three lines), Reports, then Transactions.
Match the Transaction Report date to the processor's funding date; funding is generally 1 or 2 days after the transactions.
Compare the totals.
If needed, export the report to a spreadsheet, total the dollar amounts, and compare with the funded amount.
If needed, compare transaction by transaction using the last 4 digits of the card number.
entries.quote: Funding dates are generally 1 or 2 days after transactions.
entries.note: Union's article uses CardConnect as the processor portal; a Processor Freedom merchant's funding data comes from their own processor.

entries.title: Deposits still do not match the Transaction Report
steps: The batches may be splitting, meaning batched out on more than one day.
Or the processor may be withholding funds daily instead of monthly.
Ask for help so it can be investigated.
entries.quote: your batches might be splitting (being batched out on multiple days), or the processor may be withholding funds daily instead of monthly

entries.title: Tips were not entered before End of Day was run
steps: Tips a server or bartender failed to enter before the End of Day Report was run have to be re-keyed.
Support does this, using a list of the missed tips filled in by the venue.
The process can take a couple of days.
entries.quote: This process is only necessary if the tips are not entered before the End of Day Report has processed.
entries.note: From a Union article marked INTERNAL; the re-keying itself is done by Union/processor staff.

entries.title: Find checks with tips not yet entered (Transfer Checks screen)
steps: Open the menu (three lines) and select Transfer checks.
Use the Tip Status filter: Not Entered, All, or Entered.
Other filters: Status, View (Tables, Tabs, To-Go, All) and Employee.
A check where a tip of 0.00 was entered on purpose does not count as unentered.
entries.quote: Tip Status: Not Entered, All, Entered - You can search the checks based on if tips have been entered or not
entries.note: From a Union article marked INTERNAL.

entries.title: POS on iPhone: resize or hide the menu on screen
steps: Drag the blue bar on the menu screen up or down to make the menu area larger or smaller.
Flick the menu to move it off the screen.
entries.quote: you can drag up or down the blue bar on the menu screen
entries.note: From a Union article marked INTERNAL; the only Union help article specific to POS on iPhone.

entries.title: Add a menu item
steps: Log in to the Manager Portal (needs the Edit Items and Screens permission).
Select the menu (three lines), then Inventory.
Select Add New and choose the type of item.
Fill in the item details and select Save.
Go back to Inventory and select Publish Changes to POS.
Check the change shows on a POS terminal.
entries.quote: Menu Items must be saved and published in order to appear on Union POS terminals.

entries.title: Menu changes do not show on the POS
steps: Make sure the change was saved and Publish Changes to POS was selected in the Manager Portal.
Close the Union POS app and reopen it to refresh its settings.
Repeat on any other terminals.
entries.quote: If changes do not appear on the POS terminal, close the Union POS app and reopen it to refresh its settings.

entries.title: Edit a menu item (name, price, station)
steps: Log in to the Manager Portal.
Select the menu (three lines), Inventory, then Item Management.
Search for the item and select the blue pencil icon.
Make the changes and select Save.
Select Publish Changes to POS.
entries.quote: Select the blue pencil icon next to the resulting Menu Item.

entries.title: Which printer or station an item prints to
steps: Each menu item has Item Stations: the area where its tickets print, such as a kitchen or bar station.
Change it on the item in the Manager Portal, then save and publish.
entries.quote: Add Item Stations: The area of the restaurant where the tickets related to the Menu Item will print, such as a Kitchen Station or Bar Station

entries.title: A menu screen change shows on one device size but not another
steps: A menu screen must be updated separately for each terminal size and type.
Editing the 13 inch iPad screen does not update the 10 inch, iPhone, Mobile or Online versions.
Edit each one in the Manager Portal under Inventory, Menu Set-Up, Menu Screens, then Publish Changes to POS.
entries.quote: Editing the Draft Beer menu screen for the 13" size iPad will NOT automatically update the 10", iPhone, Mobile, or Online Draft Beer menu screens.

entries.title: Set up a pricing event (for example happy hour)
steps: Log in to the Manager Portal (needs the Edit Pricing Events permission).
Select the menu (three lines), Inventory, Menu Set-Up, then Pricing Events.
Click the day the event starts and fill in name, description, time and repeat.
Tick the items to include and set the price adjustment for each.
Select Save, then Publish Changes to POS.
entries.quote: A pricing event is a scheduled date and time where selected menu items have their prices automatically updated on both Union POS Terminals and mobile apps.

entries.title: A scheduled pricing event is not showing on the POS
steps: Future pricing events do not show on the POS until their scheduled date and time.
entries.quote: Scheduled Pricing Events in future will NOT show on the POS until the specified date(s) and time(s).

entries.title: Change what a job role can do in the Manager Portal
steps: Log in to the Manager Portal.
Select the menu (three lines), Labor, then Portal Permissions.
Tick or untick boxes under each job role and select Save.
Only a job role with Modify Permissions can do this.
entries.quote: On the Labor submenu, select "Portal Permissions".

entries.title: Refunding a card payment in Union
steps: Refunds are issued from the Transaction Report in the Manager Portal.
The user's job role needs the Issue Refunds permission.
entries.quote: Issue Refunds: Allows issue of refund for a payment transaction within the Transaction Report in the Manager Portal

entries.title: Where an employee PIN code is viewed or changed
steps: Employee records in the Manager Portal hold the PIN code.
View Employee Records lets a role see it; Modify Employee Records lets a role edit it.
entries.quote: Editable values include an employee's Address, PIN Code, Job Code, Wage Rate, POS and Portal Permissions

entries.title: POS on iPhone: ways to take payment at the table
steps: Scan to pay.
Tap to pay.
Guest-led payment on the guest's own device.
entries.quote: Own Device' model      tap to pay, our guest-

entries.title: Receipt printers use thermal paper, not ink
steps: Receipt printers are thermal and need thermal paper.
They do not need ink.
entries.quote: Receipt printers are Thermal and work with Thermal paper, they do not require ink to print

entries.title: Receipt printer or cash drawer not working: check the cabling
steps: The cash drawer plugs into the printer through the RJ11/RJ12 jack; a telephone cable will not work.
The printer plugs into the POS by USB.
Make sure the power cord is pushed in properly at both ends.
entries.quote: The cash drawer plugs into the printer via the RJ11/RJ12 Jack (Telephone Style, Note: a telephone cable will not work).

entries.title: Print a test sheet from the receipt printer itself
steps: Power the printer off.
Hold the Feed button down while turning the printer back on.
If a sheet prints, the printer itself is working.
If the printer does not power on or feed paper, and it was bought from Korona, contact them for help.
entries.quote: Power down the printer. Hold the Feed button down while turning the printer back on.

entries.title: Print a test page from Windows
steps: Open Printers & Scanners in Windows.
Click the printer, then Manage.
Click Print a test page.
entries.quote: Click on the printer you are setting up and click Manage

entries.title: Printer stopped working: check Windows did not install a second copy
steps: Open Printers & Scanners in Windows.
Check whether a second copy of the printer was installed, for example 'Epson TM-T20III (2)' next to 'Epson TM-T20III'.
The printer name set in Korona must match the name in Windows exactly.
entries.quote: Check in the Printers & Scanners settings that another copy of the printer did not get installed.

entries.title: Printer works in Windows but not from Korona: check the Korona settings
steps: In KORONA Studio, Settings > POS Profile: the Printer Port should be ESC/POS or System Printer, and the variable in the Port Parameter must match.
In Sales > Point of Sale: the Printer variable's value must match the printer name in Windows exactly.
Check the POS Profile selected in Sales > Point of Sale is the one the printer was set up for.
entries.quote: The Value for the Printer variable must match the name in Windows exactly.
entries.note: Back-office configuration; a confident owner can do it, otherwise hand to POS support.

entries.title: Korona POS needs Windows 10 or above
steps: KORONA POS only works with Windows 10 and above.
entries.quote: KORONA POS only works with Windows 10 and above.

entries.title: Receipt printer not printing: basic checks
steps: Check the printer is powered on.
Press the Feed button and see whether the printer tries to feed paper.
If not, check the power cord is fully plugged in and the printer is switched on.
Check there is receipt paper in the printer.
entries.quote: When you hit the “Feed” button, does the printer try to feed the paper?

entries.title: Printer not printing: driver and Windows test print
steps: The correct driver must be installed; see Korona's Windows printer drivers and setup page, or get the driver from the printer maker's website.
Search for 'printer' in Windows system settings and run a test print.
If it prints from Windows, the driver is fine and the printer only needs configuring in KORONA Studio.
entries.quote: If the receipt printer prints from this screen, then the driver is correctly installed and the printer just needs to be configured in the KORONA Studio cloud backend.

entries.title: "unable to find valid certification path" (when installing Korona POS)
steps: This usually means the Java version on the computer is out of date.
KORONA POS uses Java 17, specifically Azul Zulu JDK FX 17.
Install the Azul Java and uninstall older versions such as Java 8.
entries.quote: sometimes the below “unable to find valid certification path” error can appear

entries.title: Check which Java version a Korona register has
steps: Type CMD in the Windows search bar and open the Command Prompt.
Type java -version; it shows the installed version.
Or look in Add or remove programs in system settings.
entries.quote: You can type ” java -version” and it will tell you the current version of Java that is installed on your computer.

entries.title: "Failed to start database"
steps: This appears when the KORONA Client is already running and a second copy is opened; only one can run at a time.
Select OK on the error box.
Look on the taskbar for the KORONA Client that is already open and use that one.
entries.quote: This error will pop up if you have the KORONA Client running in the background and you attempt to open a second KORONA Client.

entries.title: PAX S300: test the internet connection (ping)
steps: Press Menu on the PAX screen; if that fails, hold the blue FUNC button and press 1.
Enter the password. The default is today's date in MMDDYYYY format; if that is wrong, ask your provider.
Press the on-screen down arrow to the second page and select Communication.
Go to the second page again and select Lan Parameters.
Go to the second page and select Ping.
When 'google.com' shows, press the green key.
'PING OK' means the terminal is connected to the internet.
If it does not ping, check the Ethernet cable is plugged in correctly and try again.
entries.quote: If the device returns “PING OK” (see the picture to the right), the PAX s300 is successfully connected to the internet.

entries.title: Genius payment terminal: test the connection
steps: From the Genius splash screen press the 0 key three times.
Type the password and press Enter (green button). The default is 9416557; if that is wrong, contact your provider.
Touch the TEST button on the screen.
'Passed' means it is connected.
If it fails, the device needs the maintenance procedure to re-initialize it.
entries.quote: Note* The default password is 9416557. If this is incorrect, please get in touch with your provider.

entries.title: PAX A35: check it is connected to the network
steps: On the Home screen open the Settings app.
Enter the password. The default is pax9876@@; if that is wrong, contact your provider.
Select Network & Internet, then Wifi or Ethernet, whichever you use.
On Wi-Fi, select the network; it shows whether you are connected. Select Advanced to see the IP address.
On Ethernet, check there is an IP address.
As long as the IP address is not 0.0.0.0, the terminal is connected.
entries.quote: As long as your IP isn’t 0.0.0.0, you’re connected.

entries.title: Dejavoo Z11: check the Wi-Fi connection
steps: Tap the Wi-Fi icon at the top left of the terminal screen.
If the icon on the right says connected, the terminal is on Wi-Fi.
entries.quote: Step 1: Click the wifi icon in the top left of the device on this screen:

entries.title: BlockChyp terminal: getting it online
steps: Make sure it is connected with an Ethernet cable; it should go online straight away.
entries.quote: You just need to make sure they are connected via ethernet cable and it should immediately go online.

entries.title: POS stuck on the payment page with an error popup (PAX terminal)
steps: The terminal did not send the result back to the POS.
PAX terminals check for the transaction automatically when they lose connection.
If the transaction is found, the POS closes the receipt as normal.
If it is not found, the POS shows 'Transaction not found'; press the credit button again to rerun the payment.
entries.quote: PAX terminals automatically check for the transaction when they lose their connection. You don’t need to set anything up.

entries.title: "Transaction not found"
steps: The POS could not find the card payment on the terminal.
Press the credit button again to rerun the payment.
If a duplicate error then appears, the first payment did go through: do not charge again.
entries.quote: If the transaction isn’t found, the POS shows a “Transaction not found” error. The cashier should press the credit button again to rerun the payment.

entries.title: POS stuck on the payment page with an error popup (Dejavoo terminal)
steps: After the error popup, press the Dejavoo Status button on the payment page.
If the transaction is found, the POS closes the receipt as normal.
If it is not found, run the credit payment again.
entries.quote: After the error pop-up, the cashier presses “Dejavoo Status” on the payment page.
entries.note: The Dejavoo Status button must have been added to the payment layout in KORONA Studio first.

entries.title: Add the Dejavoo Status button to the payment screen
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Payment Methods and create a new payment method, named for example 'Dejavoo Status'.
Set Payment Service to Credit Terminal.
Enter DEJAVOOSTATUS in the Service Parameter field and save.
Go to Settings > Button Configurations and open your button configuration.
Open the payment layout, click Edit, click an empty slot and name the button.
Click Add Function, select Payment Method, choose Dejavoo Status and save.
At the POS, run Retrieve Master Data to see the new button.
entries.quote: Enter “DEJAVOOSTATUS” in the “Service Parameter” field.

entries.title: Duplicate error popup when re-running a card payment
steps: The first transaction did go through. Do not charge the card again.
Close out the sale with the Offline Credit payment method instead.
If there is no duplicate error, the first transaction did not go through and the new one completes as normal.
entries.quote: Duplicate error popup: the first transaction did go through. Don’t charge the card again. Close out the sale with the Offline Credit payment method instead.

entries.title: Offline Credit payment method: when to use it
steps: Offline Credit closes a receipt without sending anything to the card terminal.
Use it only when the terminal reports a duplicate, so the customer is not charged twice.
entries.quote: Use it only when the terminal reports a duplicate, so the customer isn’t charged twice.

entries.title: Set up the Offline Credit payment method
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Payment Methods and create a new payment method.
Name it clearly, for example 'Offline Credit'.
Set Payment Service to None and leave everything else at default.
Save, then add it to the payment layout as a button.
entries.quote: Set “Payment Service” to “None”. Leave all other settings at their defaults.

entries.title: Review receipts closed with Offline Credit
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Sales > Receipts and filter by the Offline Credit payment method.
Compare each receipt with your processor's portal or batch report to confirm the charge is there.
entries.quote: Compare each receipt with your processor’s portal or batch report to confirm the charge is there.

entries.title: Card terminal keeps losing connection to the POS (PAX): reserve its IP address
steps: PAX terminals often lose connection because their IP address changes.
Set up an IP reservation (DHCP reservation, also called a local static IP) for the terminal in the router's settings.
If you have an IT team or managed service provider, ask them to do it.
If you manage the router, log in to its admin portal and look for DHCP Reservation, IP Reservation or Static IP.
Your internet provider can also help set up a local DHCP reservation.
You do not need a paid public static IP.
entries.quote: PAX terminals often lose connection because their IP address changes.
entries.note: Needs router access; hand off if the merchant has no one who manages the network.

entries.title: Card terminals drop out at busy times: put POS and terminals on their own switch
steps: Terminals can disconnect when they share the network with guest Wi-Fi, smart TVs, audio systems or cameras.
Get an unmanaged gigabit switch (5 or 8 port).
Plug only the POS terminals, payment terminals and the connection from the router into it.
Keep other devices on the main router or a separate switch.
entries.quote: Plug only your POS terminals, payment terminals, and the connection from your router into the new switch.

entries.title: PAX Communication Error: first steps (terminal was working before)
steps: On screen 3 of the POS, press Retrieve Master Data and then Restart POS.
After both, cancel the first receipt.
If that does not help, unplug the PAX from power and make sure it is off.
Plug it back in and wait for the splash screen.
Then do Retrieve Master Data and Restart POS again.
entries.quote: On-screen 3, you should have ‘Retrieve Master Data’ and ‘Restart POS’ buttons.

entries.title: What a PAX Communication Error means
steps: The POS terminal cannot send payment data to the PAX device.
A main cause is that the PAX IP address is not set, or has changed, in the POS settings in KORONA Studio.
entries.quote: A PAX Communication Error occurs when the terminal cannot send payment data to the PAX Device for processing.

entries.title: PAX Communication Error: update the PAX IP address in KORONA Studio
steps: On the PAX, press Func + 1 together and enter the password you were given.
Tap Communications (the password is asked again), then LAN Parameters, then IP Address, and note the number.
In LAN Parameters check LAN Type shows 1 (DHCP).
On an Android PAX the IP shows at the top left when the app starts.
In KORONA Studio go to Sales > Points of sale and open the point of sale.
Under Device Configuration Variables, set the credit terminal variable's value to the PAX IP address.
Save the value and save the Point of Sale.
At the register, retrieve master data, restart, and run the transaction again.
entries.quote: Once inside the Point of Sale, scroll down to Device Configuration Variables and locate your credit terminal variable. The value should be the IP address of the PAX Payment Terminal.

entries.title: PAX payment settings cannot be changed by the merchant
steps: PAX payment application settings (tips, EMV, contactless limits, merchant parameters) are not available to the merchant.
They must be updated by the processor or by KORONA POS.
Batch the terminal before any settings are changed.
entries.quote: These Settings are not available to the merchant and must be updated by the Processor / KORONA POS.

entries.title: PAX: tap (contactless) payments depend on terminal settings
steps: Tap payments are controlled by the Allow Fast Payment and Contactless settings in the PAX parameters.
A Contactless Trans Limit sets a dollar limit for tap transactions.
These are changed by the processor, not the merchant.
entries.quote: Allow Fast Payment – Enabled or Disabled to allow tap payments.

entries.title: PAX: tip prompts on the card terminal are a terminal setting
steps: Tip suggestions can be switched on or off in the PAX parameters.
Three fixed amounts or three percentages can be offered.
The processor changes these, not the merchant.
entries.quote: Three Percentage Configurable Amounts – Allows setting three tip percentages for customer selection.

entries.title: Connect a PAX card terminal to Korona POS
steps: A Credit Authorization Terminal Assistant on the KORONA Studio dashboard can do this for you; use these steps if that did not work.
In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profiles and edit the profile.
Click Add Device, choose Credit Terminal as Type and PAX Credit Terminal as Device.
Add a Port and a Device Configuration Variable holding the PAX IP address.
In Settings > Payment Methods, set the credit payment method's Payment Service to Credit Terminal and Processing Type to Default.
Update master data at the register and restart the POS software.
entries.quote: Select Credit Terminal next to Type and PAX Credit Terminal next to Device, and hit OK.

entries.title: Find the IP address of a PAX terminal (Menu method)
steps: Make sure the terminal is on the same network as the POS.
Power it on and press Menu.
Enter the password; it varies and comes from the company that supplied the terminal.
Arrow down to Communication and select it; enter the password again.
Arrow down to LAN Parameters, then select IP Address.
Drop leading zeros when entering it in Korona: 010.001.000.247 becomes 10.1.0.247.
entries.quote: EXAMPLE* If your credit terminal displays 010.001.000.247, enter 10.1.0.247 into the Port Parameter field.

entries.title: Restart the POS after changing card terminal settings
steps: After changing the device profile, update master data at the register.
Then restart the POS software so the change takes effect.
entries.quote: It is necessary to restart the POS software for the change to take effect after you update the master data at checkout when making changes to the device profile.

entries.title: Connect a Dejavoo card terminal to Korona POS
steps: The Dejavoo must be boarded on the SPIN platform and you need its SPIN RegisterID and SPIN authKey.
In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profiles, edit the profile, click Add Device, choose Credit Terminal and Dejavoo Credit Terminal.
Set the Port to Network.
Check the device Settings: address, keyPassphrase (the SPIn AuthKey), RegisterId and signatureCapture. They are case sensitive.
In Sales > Points of Sale open the POS and add djvauth and djvregid under Device Configuration Variables with the SPIn keys as values.
In Settings > Payment Methods set the credit method's Payment Service to Credit Terminal and Processing Type to Default.
Run Retrieve Master Data on the POS and restart the POS software.
entries.quote: Before getting started, you must ensure that the Dejavoo device is boarded on the SPIN network platform and that you have been provided with your specific Dejavoo SPIN Registered and SPIN authKey.

entries.title: Card terminals with Korona normally batch automatically
steps: The terminals are typically set to batch automatically at a set time.
A manual batch is only needed outside the normal routine.
entries.quote: Typically, the devices are set to batch automatically at a certain time.

entries.title: Manually close the batch on a PAX S300
steps: Press Func + 1 together to open the administration menu.
Enter the password you were given.
Tap Host Settings and enter the password again.
Scroll down and tap Batch Close.
'Batch Closed' shows when it is done.
entries.quote: The S300 will process the batch. When finished will display a message stating “Batch Closed.”

entries.title: Manually close the batch on an Android PAX (A35, A77, A80, A920, Aries)
steps: Tap the four corners of the screen in order: top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left.
Enter the password you were given.
Go to Host Settings.
Press Batch Close.
entries.quote: You will need to tap the 4 corners of the screen starting in the top left and move clockwise from there.

entries.title: PAX is not batching automatically
steps: On the PAX home screen go to Settings > Security.
Set the scheduled reboot time to after your usual batch time, for example 3AM or 4AM.
entries.quote: If your device is not automatically batching frequently, go to the Pax home screen > Settings > Security and set the scheduled reboot time to after your typical batch time (3AM or 4AM for example).

entries.title: Manually settle the batch on a Dejavoo (Z11, Z9, QD4, Q-series)
steps: Press the three-lines icon at the bottom left of the screen.
Enter the password you were given (default 1234).
Go to Settlement and select Settle Daily Batch.
On some Z-series models, press the gold star icon at the bottom, enter the password, then select Settle Daily Batch.
entries.quote: From there, navigate to Settlement and select the option Settle Daily Batch

entries.title: Standalone mode: taking cards on the terminal without the POS
steps: Standalone mode lets you type a total into the card terminal without the POS being involved.
It may be needed when the internet goes out or for testing during setup.
entries.quote: This makes it so that you can manually type in a total on the credit terminal without the POS being involved.

entries.title: Put an Android PAX (A35, A60, A80, A920) in standalone mode
steps: In the payment app, tap the four corners of the screen: top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left.
Enter the password you were given (typically your street address or the current date, e.g. 05082026).
Go to System Settings and scroll to the bottom.
Set ECR-Terminal Integration Mode to Internal POS/Standalone, then exit to the payment screen.
When finished, go back and set ECR-Terminal Integration Mode to External POS again.
entries.quote: The third option from the bottom, ECR-Terminal Integration Mode, needs to be set to Internal POS/Standalone.

entries.title: Put a Dejavoo QD4 in standalone mode (SPIn bypass)
steps: In the payment app, find the icon with a circle and a bent line around it (second from the left).
Press it to enter or leave standalone mode.
entries.quote: Inside the payment app, there is an icon with a circle and a bent line around it (second from the left).

entries.title: Put a Dejavoo Z11 or Z9 in standalone mode (SPIN bypass)
steps: Press the gold star icon at the bottom.
Enter the manager password (default 1234) and press the green button.
Select Turn SPIN Bypass On.
This allows one standalone transaction, then bypass turns off again.
To leave bypass on permanently, contact whoever programmed the terminal.
entries.quote: This will allow you to do a standalone transaction once, and then it will default back to SPIN bypass to off.

entries.title: Key in a card number by hand on a PAX
steps: When the PAX prompts to swipe, type the card number instead.
The terminal then asks for the expiry date and the CVV/CSC.
The card number is required; the other items can be skipped with the green enter button if not available.
entries.quote: To enter the manual payment, enter the card number when prompted to swipe. The device will prompt you for the rest.

entries.title: PAX will not allow manual card entry
steps: Manual entry may be disabled on the terminal.
The MOTO setting in the device parameters has to be changed by whoever supplied the terminal.
entries.quote: They should be able to adjust the “MOTO” setting in the device parameters.

entries.title: Set a static IP on an Android PAX (Ethernet)
steps: Open Settings and enter the PAX password (default pax9876@@).
Tap Ethernet and enable it.
Scroll to the bottom and tap Ethernet Configuration.
Select Static IP.
Enter the IP address, netmask, gateway and DNS server.
Save.
entries.quote: scroll down to the botton and tap Ethernet Configuration
entries.note: Needs the network's addressing details; hand off unless the merchant has IT help.

entries.title: Set a static IP on an Android PAX (Wi-Fi)
steps: Open Settings and enter the PAX password (default pax9876@@).
Select Wi-Fi and turn it on.
Select the network and enter its password.
Open Advanced Options, select IP settings, then Static.
Enter the IP address, gateway, network prefix and DNS server.
Press Connect.
entries.quote: Enter PAX default password – pax9876@@
entries.note: Needs the network's addressing details; hand off unless the merchant has IT help.

entries.title: PAX S300: find its current IP address
steps: Press Menu on the PAX screen; if that fails, hold the blue FUNC button and press 1.
Enter the password (default: today's date as MMDDYYYY; otherwise ask your provider).
Go to the second page of the menu and select Communication.
Go to the second page and select Lan Parameters.
Go to the second page and select IP Address.
entries.quote: Press the Down Arrow from the Lan Parameters Options to view the second page and select IP Address.

entries.title: PAX A series: find its current IP address
steps: Tap the Settings gear on the PAX home screen.
Enter the password: by default 9876 or pax9876@@; if neither works try today's date as MMDDYYYY, then ask your provider.
Go to Network & Internet, then Ethernet or Wifi.
For Wi-Fi select Advanced; for Ethernet select Ethernet.
Write down the IP address shown.
entries.quote: By default, all PAX passwords are either “9876” or “pax9876@@”.

entries.title: PAX shows IP address 0.0.0.0
steps: The PAX is not connected to the internet.
Check its network connection.
entries.quote: If the IP address says 0.0.0.0, your PAX is not connected to the internet and you will need check

entries.title: Card terminal stopped talking to the POS after its IP changed
steps: Note the PAX's current IP address.
In KORONA Studio go to the Sales tab, then Points of Sale, and open the POS the terminal belongs to.
Under Device Configuration Variable, find the 'PAX' variable and replace the old IP address in Value with the new one.
Confirm, then Save under Edit Point of Sale.
At the register run Retrieve Master Data (Update POS).
Run a test transaction.
If it still fails, contact support.
entries.quote: You will want to edit the Value and replace the old IP address with the new one.

entries.title: PAX A35: unbox and cable it
steps: Plug the USB-A end of the separate USB-C to USB-A cable into the wall power adapter.
Plug its USB-C end into the solid block in the middle of the multi-cable.
Plug the multi-cable's single USB-C lead (sloped plastic end) into the back of the A35.
For wired internet, plug the Ethernet cable into the Ethernet port on the multi-cable (red connector).
For Wi-Fi, connect after power-on from the Settings app.
Plug into power; the PAX turns on by itself.
entries.quote: Attach the singular USB-C cable that comes off of the multi-cable, the plastic end to the connector is sloped in shape, into the back of the PAX A35.

entries.title: The PAX does not plug into the register
steps: The PAX does not connect directly to the POS in any way.
All communication between them goes over the network.
entries.quote: All communication between the PAX and the POS happens over the network connection.

entries.title: New Korona account: add the PAX to the POS profile
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Sales > Points of Sale and open the POS to see which POS Profile it uses.
Go to Settings > POS Profiles and open that profile.
Under Devices, add a Credit Terminal if there is none.
Back in Sales > Points of Sale, add the Device Configuration Variable.
Enter the PAX's IP address.
entries.quote: If you do not see a section under devices called “Credit Terminal” you will need to add one as shown below:

entries.title: Set up a PAX with the Credit Authorization Terminal Assistant
steps: On the KORONA Studio Dashboard, open the Credit Authorization Terminal Assistant in the Getting Started box.
Choose PAX Terminal and click Continue.
Choose the POS Profile (one, or all).
Choose Network as the connection type, enter the terminal's IP address in the Port field and click Continue.
If asked, enter a terminal password, say whether a POS printer is used, and choose the printer width.
Click Save, then Close.
entries.quote: The easiest way to set up your credit card terminal is to use the Credit Authorization Terminal Assistant, a wizard located in the Getting Started box on your Dashboard in KORONA Studio.

entries.title: A card terminal is linked to a POS Profile, not to one register
steps: The credit terminal stays linked to a specific POS Profile, not to a POS itself.
entries.quote: The credit terminal will stay linked to a specific POS Profile and not a POS itself.

entries.title: KORONA POS maker support: phone, email and hours
steps: KORONA's direct support line is +1 (702) 997-7672.
Email is support@koronapos.com; describe the problem and include your login email, never your password.
General support is Monday to Friday, 6 AM to 6 PM Pacific.
Emergency support is 24/7/365 for anything that stops sales or normal business.
entries.quote: Emergency support: 24/7/365 for anything that prevents clients from making sales or conducting normal business operations.
entries.note: Maker's own line; Processor Freedom Point of Sale Support is the merchant's first contact.

entries.title: KORONA general support hours
steps: Monday through Friday, 6 AM to 6 PM Pacific time.
entries.quote: General support: Monday through Friday from 6AM to 6 PM PT.

entries.title: KORONA support never asks for your password
steps: Do not give your password to anyone claiming to be support.
Do not include it in emails.
entries.quote: Please note, KORONA Support will never ask for your password.

entries.title: KORONA live chat
steps: Live chat is the orange chat bubble at the bottom right of the KORONA manual site.
Enter name, email and a short message and click Submit.
entries.quote: Look for the orange chat bubble in the bottom right corner of the page.

entries.title: Send a support request from KORONA Studio
steps: In KORONA Studio open the welcome menu at the top left.
Select Support to open the contact form and answer its questions.
entries.quote: Selecting “Support” opens the support contact form.

entries.title: Turn on remote support at the register
steps: Tap the KORONA logo at the top left of the POS to open the info page.
In the bottom toolbar press Activate Remote Support.
On Windows registers TeamViewer opens; give the support agent your partner ID and password.
If TeamViewer shows no password, download a new version from the Windows Support link at the top of the KORONA manual site.
entries.quote: In the bottom toolbar, you will find a large button in the middle labeled “Activate Remote Support.”

entries.title: Korona's list of payment processor support numbers
steps: Korona publishes support contacts for commonly used processors: TSYS, First Data, Priority/Bold, Heartland, Cayan Genius, Clearent, Elavon and Evo.
entries.quote: Here is contact information for some of the most commonly used payment processors.
entries.note: Processor Freedom merchants should be sent to Processor Freedom support, not to these numbers.

entries.title: Enter the starting cash balance at the start of the day
steps: Open the Number 3 side menu and press Starting Balance/Cash Deposit.
Enter the amount.
Press Enter (arrow icon); the amount appears on the receipt.
Finish it like a normal cash transaction; a receipt prints confirming the starting balance.
entries.quote: Navigate to the Starting Balance/ Cash Deposit button located in the Number 3 side menu.

entries.title: End of day at the register (Balance POS/End of Day)
steps: Open the Number 3 side menu and select Balance POS/End of Day.
Count all the cash in the drawer and enter the amount.
The system tells you if the amount is incorrect.
entries.quote: Navigate back to the Number 3 side menu and select Balance POS/End of Day. You will be prompted to enter the amount in your drawer.

entries.title: Ring up a sale
steps: Add the products.
Press Total to go to the payment screen.
Choose a payment method (Cash, Credit, etc.) to complete the sale.
entries.quote: Choose a payment method (Cash, Credit, etc.) to complete the transaction.

entries.title: Search for a product at the register
steps: Press the 2 icon at the top right of the screen to open the sidebar.
Press Product Search.
For one item, click Add Item & Close.
For several, highlight each product and click Select Product; on the last one click Add Item & Close.
entries.quote: Select the 2 icon at the top-right of your screen to open the sidebar with the Product Search button.

entries.title: Receipt archive shows only the 15 most recent receipts
steps: The receipt archive at the register lists the 15 most recent receipts.
Older receipts can still be pulled up by scanning the customer's receipt or typing the receipt number.
Receipt numbers are in KORONA Studio under Sales > Receipts.
entries.quote: In the receipt archive, you will see your 15 most recent receipts displayed on the screen.

entries.title: Take part cash and the rest on a card
steps: On the payment screen enter the cash amount (for example 5) and press Cash.
The rest shows as the balance owed.
Press Credit to charge the remaining balance to a card.
entries.quote: Select Credit to charge the remaining $15 to a card.

entries.title: Do not change the default payment method from Cash
steps: The default payment method on a point of sale is Cash.
Changing it alters many functions and is likely to cause problems.
entries.quote: Additionally, your default payment method is Cash. Please do not change this, as it will change numerous functions in your point of sale and will likely cause difficulties later on.

entries.title: Change the receipt header or footer
steps: In KORONA Studio open the point of sale under Sales > Points of Sale.
The receipt header and footer are on the right side of the point of sale page.
entries.quote: You can find the receipt header and footer on the right side of each point of sale page

entries.title: Where to find past end-of-day statements and receipts
steps: End-of-day statements and all receipts are in KORONA Studio under Sales.
Receipts can be filtered there.
entries.quote: Additionally, all receipts can be found under Sales and at the bottom of the list.

entries.title: Cashier login codes
steps: Each cashier has their own login code, which records who finalized each receipt.
The default cashier login code is 1.
Codes are added or changed in KORONA Studio (Create Cashiers).
entries.quote: *The default cashier login code is “1.”

entries.title: Log out or switch cashier
steps: Press Logout (by default under function tab 1) to return to the login screen.
The current transaction stays open and resumes when the cashier logs back in.
entries.quote: If a cashier logs out, the current transaction remains open and will resume as soon as the cashier logs back in.

entries.title: Cashier Pause locks the register to one cashier
steps: The Cashier Pause button logs out quickly.
While paused, no other cashier can log in.
entries.quote: This function will disallow any other cashiers from logging in.

entries.title: A cashier sees someone else's open transaction after logging in
steps: Cashiers with the Foreign Receipt permission resume the most recent transaction even if it is not theirs.
They can also open a list of open receipts with the Open Receipt via Order Number function.
entries.quote: Cashiers with the “Foreign Receipt” permission will resume automatically with the most recent transaction, even if it is not theirs.

entries.title: Logging in at the register
steps: The login screen asks for a PIN.
If a password has been set, the cashier is asked for that password too.
entries.quote: Cashiers will first see a login screen requiring a PIN.

entries.title: Change the quantity of an item
steps: Select the item on the receipt.
Key in the quantity you want.
Press Change Quantity.
entries.quote: To change the quantity of an item, press the amount you want to change the quantity to after selecting the item on the receipt, and then hit ‘Change Quantity‘.

entries.title: What Balance, Cash Deposit, Cash Drop, Retrieve Master Data and Restart do
steps: Balance is for the end of the day.
Cash Deposit is for the beginning balance.
Cash drop takes cash out of the drawer to lower its balance or pay vendors.
Retrieve Master Data brings changes made in the cloud to the POS.
Restart restarts the POS.
entries.quote: Cash drop is to take cash out of the drawer to reduce the balance of the drawer or pay vendors.

entries.title: Changes made in the back office are not showing at the register
steps: Press Retrieve Master Data at the register; it brings changes made in the cloud to the POS.
entries.quote: Retrieve Master Data brings changes made on the cloud to the POS.

entries.title: Return items when the customer has the receipt
steps: Open the Receipt Archive and press Return Page.
Scan the receipt, type its number, or pick it from the list.
Use the plus and minus keys to choose the items and quantities being returned.
Press Return of Goods.
Press Total, choose the payment type for the refund, and press Enter.
entries.quote: Once the selection for return has been completed, press Return of Goods to continue the return.

entries.title: Exchange: return items and sell others in one transaction
steps: Start the return from the Receipt Archive as usual.
Ring in the new items as normal, then press Total.
The payment screen shows the difference, either a refund to the customer or an amount due.
entries.quote: On the payment screen, the POS will show the difference due, either in the form of a refund to the customer or payment due from the customer.

entries.title: Return items without a receipt
steps: Only if store policy allows it.
Ring in the items being returned and press the Return button (typically on functions page 2).
The total shows as a negative number, the amount due back to the customer.
The receipt gets a Signature line and a Reason line.
entries.quote: Enter the items the customer wants to return to the POS and press the Return button.

entries.title: Pressed the Return button by mistake
steps: Cancel the entire receipt.
Cancelling only the items leaves the signature and reason lines on the receipt.
entries.quote: If you touch the return button by mistake, you must cancel the entire receipt because if you only cancel the items, the signature and reason lines will still appear on the receipt.

entries.title: Void a finished receipt
steps: Open the receipt archive.
Select the receipt from the list or enter its number.
Press Void Receipt.
If there is a receipt printer, a void receipt prints.
entries.quote: Once you have selected the receipt, you can use the “Void Receipt” button to void the receipt.

entries.title: Cannot void a receipt
steps: Only cashiers with the Void Receipt permission can void.
Only receipts from the current business day (z-count) can be voided.
Once Finish Day has been run, do a return instead.
entries.quote: This means, once the finish day has been performed, the receipts can no longer be voided.

entries.title: Cancel an open (unfinished) receipt
steps: Use Cancel Receipt to get out of a transaction that has not been finalized.
If the receipt already has credit or gift card payments on it, void or remove those payments first; the POS will not void them for you.
Cancellations can be reviewed in KORONA Studio under Sales > Receipts.
entries.quote: make sure to void/remove the payments before canceling the receipt because the POS will not try to void them

entries.title: Reopen a finished receipt to fix the payment method or add a tip
steps: Open the receipt archive and select the receipt (from the list, or by entering or scanning its number).
Press Reopen Receipt; the payment screen opens.
Remove or adjust payments, or add new payments.
Items cannot be added or removed this way; do returns and add-on sales as a new transaction.
entries.quote: The function cannot be used to add or remove items from a sale. Item returns and “add on” sales must be performed in a new transaction.

entries.title: Repeat a previous sale (Copy Receipt)
steps: Open the receipt archive and select the receipt.
Press Copy Receipt; a new transaction opens with the same items.
Change it if needed, then close the sale.
entries.quote: Once the receipt is selected you can use the copy receipt button which will create a new transaction with the same line items.

entries.title: Return items using Copy Receipt
steps: Copy the original receipt from the receipt archive.
Remove the items that are not being returned.
Press Return; the receipt becomes a return transaction.
entries.quote: Then press the Return button which will turn the receipt into a return transaction.

entries.title: Put a sale on hold (Park Receipt)
steps: Press Park Receipt; the register starts a new transaction.
When that transaction is finished, the parked receipt comes back automatically if it has no order number.
Several parked receipts come back in the order they were parked.
entries.quote: In order to put the current transaction on hold, simply press the Park Receipt button, which will take the cashier into a new transaction.

entries.title: Bring back a parked receipt
steps: Press the P parked receipts icon at the top right of the POS.
Select the receipt in the list and press Enter.
entries.quote: To open a parked receipt, you can press the P parked receipts icon at the top right of the POS.

entries.title: Find an old receipt at the register
steps: Press Show Receipt Archive.
The list shows receipt number, date, cashier and amount.
For older receipts, enter or scan the receipt number.
From there you can print, copy or reopen the receipt.
entries.quote: It can also be used to recall older receipts by entering or scanning the receipt number.

entries.title: Print a gift receipt
steps: In the receipt archive, select the receipt and press Print Gift Receipt.
Gift receipts hide all prices.
entries.quote: Gift receipts hide all prices and are usually only printed on customer request.
entries.note: The button must have been added to the receipt archive layout in KORONA Studio.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt
steps: Open the receipt archive, select the receipt and press Print to print a copy.
Print also works from the booking screen and the total screen for the current receipt.
entries.quote: It can be used from the booking screen, total screen or in the receipt archive to print a copy of a previous receipt.

entries.title: Turn automatic receipt printing on or off
steps: Tap the printer icon in the status bar.
Blue means receipts print automatically; grey means they do not.
entries.quote: If the icon is blue, the receipt print is enabled.  If the icon is grey, the receipt print is disabled.

entries.title: Receipts print even though printing is turned off
steps: The payment method used has a forced receipt print.
Change that option in KORONA Studio under Settings > Payment Methods.
entries.quote: If the POS prints a receipt even though the receipt print is disabled, then the selected payment method has a forced receipt print.

entries.title: Cash drawer is not opening
steps: The drawer and receipt printer work together; if one fails the other usually does too.
Check the drawer is plugged into the receipt printer and the printer is connected to the POS.
Check the printer is on and has paper.
Press the feed button and see that paper feeds.
Try printing a test page.
Fix whichever of these fails, then try the drawer again.
entries.quote: The cash drawer and the receipt printer work in tandem. If one isn’t working, typically the other won’t work either.

entries.title: Cash drawer clicks but does not open
steps: The drawer is locked with its physical key.
Unlock it and try again.
entries.quote: If so, the drawer is locked with the physical keys that came with the drawer. Unlock it and try again.

entries.title: The Open Cash Drawer button
steps: Open Cash Drawer opens the drawer at any time and needs no permission or payment.
It can be used to test that the drawer is set up correctly.
entries.quote: Please be aware that this function does not require any permissions or payments.

entries.title: See the register's identity and configuration (KORONA POS Info)
steps: Touch the KORONA POS logo at the top left of the POS screen.
The page shows the POS identity and configuration and has the option to enable remote support.
entries.quote: This function is always available by touching the KORONA POS logo in the top left corner of the POS screen.

entries.title: Split a sale across more than one payment
