steps: Press Total to go to the payment screen.
Press Split Payment (set to credit unless changed), key in the amount for the first card and press Enter.
The remaining total shows on the entry line; repeat for another partial card payment.
For the remainder on a card, press Credit, then Enter.
For the remainder in cash, press Cash; if the customer hands over more, key that amount first, then Cash.
When the total is covered, the sale completes.
entries.quote: After pressing the button then press the amount you want to charge to the credit card and press ‘enter’.

entries.title: Get a tip prompt on the card terminal
steps: Tip prompting has to be switched on at the card terminal itself; the card processor enables it.
Once enabled, in KORONA Studio go to Settings > Payment Methods, select Credit, enter 'tips' under Service Parameter and Save.
entries.quote: To get a prompt on your credit card terminal asking customers if they would like to tip, you must activate this option on the credit card terminal itself. Your credit card payment processor can enable it.

entries.title: Add a tip from a signed paper receipt after the sale (tip adjust)
steps: Complete the credit sale at the POS.
Open the Receipt Archive, find the receipt and press Reopen Receipt (change payment).
On the payment screen enter the tip amount.
Press the tip adjustment button set up for your card terminal.
The transaction closes and the receipt shows the adjusted total.
entries.quote: Go to the Receipt Archive, find the receipt, and then press the Reopen Receipt (change payment) button. This will take you to the payment screen
entries.note: Needs the tip adjustment button and 'printtip' service parameter set up first.

entries.title: Set up tip adjust for a PAX terminal
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Payment Methods > Credit and add 'printtip' to the Service Parameter line.
In button configurations create a button named Tip Adjustment on the payment screen.
Add these functions in order: Account – Tips; Payment method – Credit; Function – Adjust Payment.
entries.quote: This will send the adjusted amount to the credit card terminal and process that adjusted tip amount.

entries.title: Set up tip adjust for a Dejavoo terminal
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Payment Methods > Credit and add 'printtip' to the Service Parameter line.
Create a button with the functions: Account – Tips/Gratuity; Function – Adjust Payment.
entries.quote: Go to Settings > Payment Methods > Credit, and then add “printtip” to the Service Parameter line of the payment method.

entries.title: What the end-of-day statement (z-tape) is
steps: It summarises all activity for one register for one business day (z-count period).
Once finished at the POS, a finalized z-count cannot be changed; its sales are final.
entries.quote: Once completed on the POS, a finalized z-count can not be modified. Sales within the z-count are all final.

entries.title: Balance shows zero after end of day
steps: When you balance or finish the day, the balance in KORONA POS resets to zero.
The same happens each time Balance Cashier is used.
entries.quote: When you balance/finish day on your POS, the balance in KORONA POS will reset to zero.

entries.title: Balance POS already finishes the day
steps: Balance POS automatically performs Finish Day after balancing.
Do not run Finish Day again afterwards.
entries.quote: There is no need to perform the finish day function additionally after using POS balance.

entries.title: A cashier cannot ring sales after balancing
steps: After a cashier runs Balance Cashier they cannot do more transactions until Finish Day has been run.
Run Finish Day at the end of the business day, after all cashiers have balanced.
entries.quote: Once a cashier has performed their balance, they will not be able to perform any more transactions until the Finish Day function has been performed.

entries.title: Close the register without counting the drawer (Finish Day)
steps: Press the Finish Day button.
The POS finalizes all sales and resets the cash drawer balance to 0.
entries.quote: By pressing the Finish Day button, the POS will increase its internal z-count and finalize all sales. The cash drawer balance will be reset back to 0.

entries.title: Set an automatic end of day
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profiles, select the profile, and enable Automatic End of Day.
Enter the time in 24-hour form.
If the register is off at that time, end of day runs when it is next turned on.
entries.quote: If the point of sale is turned off at that time, the end-of-day will be performed once the POS is turned on again.

entries.title: Stop the end-of-day statement from printing
steps: By default the statement prints if a printer is configured.
Turn off the print-out for the end-of-day statement and balance statement in KORONA Studio under Settings > POS Profiles.
entries.quote: However, you can deactivate the print out for both the end-of-day statement and balance statement under Settings > POS Profiles.

entries.title: End-of-day statement: Expected, Actual and Difference
steps: Expected is what KORONA POS thinks you should have; Actual is what the cashier entered; Difference is the gap.
With integrated card payments this should only matter for cash.
Cash drops to the safe or to pay a vendor change the Expected cash.
entries.quote: Thus, if your cashier used a cash drop to remove money from the drawer to put in a safe or pay a vendor, your Expected balance will be affected.

entries.title: End-of-day statement: amounts in parentheses
steps: In Income/Expenses, an amount in parentheses is negative: money leaving KORONA POS.
entries.quote: If it’s in parentheses that indicates that the balance is negative and money is leaving KORONA POS.

entries.title: End-of-day statement: Cashier Actions lines
steps: Receipts Finished: receipts processed.
Receipts Removed: voids.
Return Goods: returns.
Receipt Cancellations: cancelled receipts.
Item Cancellations: items removed from receipts.
entries.quote: Item Cancellations – Items removed from receipts

entries.title: Balance one cashier's drawer at the end of a shift
steps: Select Cashier Balance.
Type the total cash amount, press Enter, then Apply.
By default there are 3 attempts; each wrong entry shows how many are left.
If the last attempt is still wrong, the system accepts it with the discrepancy and notifies you.
entries.quote: If the amount is still incorrect on the last attempt, the system will accept the entry with discrepancies and notify you.

entries.title: Balance Cashier is not the same as Balance POS
steps: Balance Cashier covers only that cashier's sales and does not end the business day.
That cashier cannot ring again until a full Finish Day is done.
Korona recommends an automatic end of day set for after the last cashier balances.
entries.quote: This is not the same function as POS balance, which will end the entire business day.

entries.title: Balance the drawer and end the day (Balance POS)
steps: Press Balance POS (by default on the third functions page on the right).
Type the total cash counted, press Enter, then Apply at the bottom right.
It is a blind count by default: the expected amount is not shown.
An end-of-day report prints automatically afterwards.
entries.quote: They will type in the total amount using the number pad at the bottom, then press enter (you will see the amount entered on the left), and finally press the Apply button in the bottom right.

entries.title: Balance POS says the amount does not match
steps: The POS expects the exact cash amount, to the penny.
By default there are three attempts; after the third it completes anyway and the discrepancy shows on the End of Day Statement.
An acceptable difference can be set in KORONA Studio under Settings > Payment Methods > Cash > Allowed Balance Difference.
The number of attempts is under Settings > POS Profiles, Maximum Balance Attempts.
entries.quote: If the amount does not match after three attempts, the function will complete anyway and the discrepancy will be shown on the End of Day Statement.

entries.title: Check the cash in the drawer from the back office
steps: The POS Balance Widget on the KORONA Studio dashboard shows the current cash in the drawer.
It resets each time Balance POS is done.
entries.quote: This allows you to check the cash drawer balance from the KORONA Studio when you are away from the POS.

entries.title: Count a drawer away from the register (Central Balance)
steps: At the POS press Central Balance (one cashier) or Central Balance POS (whole register).
The system logs you out and prints a small receipt.
On a PC browser open the Central Balance web page for your cloud instance (167, 185 or 420, as shown in your back-office address).
Scan or type the Receipt Barcode Number and Login Code.
Enter the actual amount and a comment, and print the finalized statement if wanted.
Click Logout.
entries.quote: Once the button is pressed, the system will automatically log you out and a small receipt will print.

entries.title: Central Balance does not show on the register's end-of-day statement
steps: It is balanced in the cloud and is not sent back to the POS.
Find these statements in KORONA Studio under Sales > Balance Statements.
entries.quote: As this is balanced in the cloud and does not communicate back to the POS, this balance will not be reflected on the POS end-of-day statement.

entries.title: Count the drawer by bills and coins (Denominated Balance)
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Payment Methods > Cash, turn on Denominated Balance and Save.
For the starting balance, go to Settings > Accounts > Cash Deposit, tick Denominated Input and Save.
At the register, key the number of each bill or coin, then press that denomination.
A receipt of the count prints when finished.
entries.quote: To enable Denominated Balance for Balance POS/End of Day, navigate to Settings>Payment Methods>Cash and then turn on Denominated Balance.

entries.title: Let cashiers see how much the drawer is over or short
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profiles and select the profile.
In the Balance section, enable Disable Blind Balance.
Left unticked, cashiers see no differences while balancing.
entries.quote: When enabled, the system shows how much the drawer is over or short during the balance process.

entries.title: How long a product import takes
steps: Imports take 24 to 48 hours during the business week.
KORONA Support replies to your original email when the import is finished.
entries.quote: Imports can take anywhere from 24-48 hours during the business week.

entries.title: Find the receipt and transaction details to answer a chargeback
steps: The bank's notice usually gives a rough time, the last 4 digits of the card, credit or debit, and the amount.
In KORONA Studio open the Evaluations tab and the Payment Transactions report.
Filter by date and payment method (Debit or Credit) and find the transaction by its total.
You typically need the Transaction Token and a copy of the receipt.
entries.quote: To answer the dispute, you will typically need the Transaction Token and a copy of the Receipt.
entries.note: The dispute itself is a money matter for client services.

entries.title: Receipt logo: image size and file type
steps: Size: 100x100px minimum, 300x300px best, 1000x1000px maximum.
Square (1:1) works best.
Use .png; .jpg may work but is not recommended.
Maximum file size 1mb.
White background, black and white image.
entries.quote: .png (.jpg may work but not recommended)

entries.title: Change what prints on the receipt
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Receipt Layouts to add a logo at the top or bottom and choose what information shows.
To add text at the top or bottom, go to Sales > Points of Sale, open the point of sale, and use the two fields under Receipt on the right.
entries.quote: You can add a logo or change what is viewed on the receipt by going to Settings > Receipt Layouts.

entries.title: Korona subscription and billing details
steps: Subscription and payment details are in KORONA Studio under 'My KORONA.studio Packages', in the sidebar section showing your name.
Change Credit Card changes the payment details.
Contact support before reducing the number of points of sale.
entries.quote: All of your subscription and payment information can be found in the “My KORONA.studio Packages” section.
entries.note: Processor Freedom merchants may be billed through Processor Freedom rather than directly; check before pointing them here.

entries.title: Card terminals Korona works with
steps: Korona has semi-integrations with PAX, Dejavoo and BlockChyp card terminals.
entries.quote: We have semi-integrations with PAX, Dejavoo, and Blockchyp credit terminals which allows us to work with most processors.

entries.title: Korona revenue does not match the processor batch or bank deposit
steps: Korona ends the day and reports revenue for that day, but the card batch happens afterwards and the deposit arrives at least a day later.
Adjust the dates you are comparing and check again.
If it still does not match, email support with the report used and the numbers that differ.
entries.quote: This is typically because KORONA ends the day and reports the revenue for the day of, but your batches won’t happen until after that and you won’t see the money deposited until at least the next day.

entries.title: Reset a forgotten KORONA Studio password
steps: Go to the KORONA Studio login screen.
Click the 'Forgot Password?' link.
entries.quote: If you forgot your password or need to reset it, go the KORONA Studio login screen and click the “Forgot Password?” link.

entries.title: Change the KORONA Studio login email
steps: Log in to KORONA Studio.
Open My User Account in the menu.
Click Request Email Change and fill in the form.
entries.quote: To change your email, log into KORONA Studio and navigate to My User Account in the menu, then click Request Email Change and fill out the form.

entries.title: How long Korona keeps sales data
steps: Sales data for active accounts is stored for 10 years.
Inactive accounts can be accessed for up to 12 months after expiry.
entries.quote: Sales data for active accounts is stored for 10 years.

entries.title: Green and yellow icons at the top right: a software update is ready
steps: The green icon with a loading arrow means the POS has downloaded the latest version from the cloud.
Press the yellow icon to install it.
The POS reboots and carries out the update.
entries.quote: To perform the update, press the yellow icon. The POS then reboots and executes the update.

entries.title: "Permission Denied" on dashboard widgets (KORONA Studio)
steps: Your user role lacks the right to display organizational units.
If you can edit user roles: Employees > User Roles > Edit Roles > Settings > Organizational Units > List Organizational Units.
If you cannot, ask your manager or supervisor to edit the role.
entries.quote: If you don’t see the widgets on the front page of the cloud, the permissions are missing, and you do not have the right to display organizational units.

entries.title: Keep a product out of price rules and promotions
steps: Price rules and promotions have no exclude option.
Either turn off Is Discountable on the product (it then cannot be discounted at all).
Or build a promotion tag containing every item to discount except the ones to exclude.
entries.quote: Price rules and promotions do not have an option to exclude certain products.

entries.title: Receipt discount is a cent or so different from what was entered
steps: A receipt discount is divided evenly across the items, so rounding can change it by one to four cents.
Example: $1 across three items gives a $0.99 discount.
entries.quote: The deviation, which is usually no more than one to four cents, is that the discount on the individual items must be divided evenly.

entries.title: A discount or promotion is not applying
steps: Check the product is eligible.
Check the promotion has the correct tag, date and customer group.
entries.quote: Check to see if the product is eligible and review your promotion to ensure you have set up the correct tag, date, and customer group.

entries.title: Put a loyalty card on a sale
steps: Key the card number on the POS keypad (phone numbers are a popular choice).
Press Set Loyalty Card; the number is applied to the receipt.
After the sale is closed the number collects points and syncs to the back office.
If a customer is on the same receipt, the customer becomes tied to that loyalty card.
entries.quote: then press the Set Loyalty Card button and this number will be applied to the receipt as its loyalty card

entries.title: Surcharging, cash discount and dual pricing options in Korona
steps: Options: surcharge or non-cash adjustment through the card terminal; Korona adding a percentage to card payments; dual pricing; or credit base prices with a cash discount.
Which to use depends on the compliance needed with the payment processor.
Setup is done with support.
entries.quote: Depending on what compliance you need with your payment processor, we can display (or not display) the surcharge or cash discount differently.

entries.title: Give a manual discount at the register
steps: A discount button must exist: Receipt Discount Absolute ($ off the receipt), Receipt Discount Percent (% off the receipt) or Sale Item Discount Absolute ($ off the selected item).
Type the discount amount on the keypad, then press the discount button.
The product must have Is Discountable enabled.
entries.quote: you can type in the desired discount amount onto the receipt keypad and then select the discount button

entries.title: Printing is off (grey icon) but some receipts still print
steps: Turning printing off only affects normal transactions.
Reprints and voided transactions always print.

These also print: balance, reports, end of day, cancelled receipts, returns, promotion coupons, gift card balance receipts, payment methods that force printing (credit cards, gift cards), production slips (kitchen, ticket, gift cards), and clock in/out slips.
entries.quote: Deactivating the printer from the POS is only for normal transactions. Reprints and voided transactions will print no matter what.

entries.title: Set all inventory counts to zero
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Inventory > Inventories and create an annual inventory count.
Select the organizational units and click Edit Inventory Count List, then Book.
On the Validate Inventory Count page choose 'Set Zero for Actual Goods' under Actions for Missing Entries.
Click Book.
entries.quote: Locate the Actions for Missing Entries drop-down menu and choose ‘Set Zero for Actual Goods.’

entries.title: New stock order from the order portal is missing from the list
steps: There is already an open stock order for the same supplier; the system updates that one instead of creating a new one.
Finalize or delete open stock orders for a new one to appear.
entries.quote: If there is an existing unbooked stock order, the system will update the open order rather than create a new one.

entries.title: PDF labels print blurry from Firefox
steps: Open the print settings in Firefox.
Under Image Quality change 600dpi to HQ1200dpi.
entries.quote: Navigate to the print settings in Firefox, go to Image Quality and change it from 600dpi to HQ1200dpi.

entries.title: Do a first inventory count
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Inventory > Inventories and press New.
Give it a description and move the organizational unit to the Selected side.
Choose Annual Inventory (loads all products) or Inventory Sampling (a blank list you add or scan into).
Press Save to keep progress; press Book to finalize the quantities.
entries.quote: Press “Save” at any time to save your progress and come back later. Press “Book” when you are finished and want to finalize the quantities.

entries.title: Stock level cannot be edited on the product page
steps: Korona tracks stock changes for history, so the level is not an editable field on the product.
Change stock through an inventory count or a stock receipt, and book it.
entries.quote: The stock level needs to be changed through an inventory or stock receipt so that the quantity of the product can be tracked at all times.

entries.title: Receive stock (create a stock receipt)
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Inventory > Stock Receipts and press +New.
Create it from a stock order, or use an empty stock receipt for goods that were not ordered in the system.
Select the target warehouse and supplier, add the products, enter purchase price and quantity received.
Book it; nothing changes until the receipt is booked.
entries.quote: A stock order does not affect inventory until you book a stock receipt for it.

entries.title: Using the register with no connection to the cloud
steps: The POS terminal can be used temporarily without the cloud connection.

These do not work offline: retrieving master data; sending sales data to the cloud; creating, checking or paying with prepaid/gift cards; inventory receipts; customer orders, offers, rentals and delivery notes; creating or looking up customers; external system calls; event ticket sales.
entries.quote: Yes, you can temporarily use the POS Terminal without connecting to the cloud. Please note, however, that certain functions only work with an active connection to the cloud.

entries.title: Gift cards cannot be sold, checked or redeemed while offline
steps: Creating, checking the balance of, and paying with prepaid/gift cards needs an active connection to the cloud.
Restore the internet connection and try again.
entries.quote: Creation, balance checking, and payments made with prepaid/gift cards.

entries.title: New product or price not showing at the register
steps: Any change made in KORONA Studio needs Retrieve Master Data (Update POS) at the register before it shows.
Example: a new product cannot be searched at the POS until Retrieve Master Data has been run.
entries.quote: Any changes that you make in the KORONA Studio Cloud Backend will require you to Retrieve Master Data (Update POS) in order to sync the Point of Sale with the Cloud.

entries.title: Products cannot be created at the register
steps: Products can only be created in the back office.
entries.quote: Products can only be created in the backend to avoid accidental or unsupervised product creation on the POS.

entries.title: Deactivated versus delisted products
steps: A deactivated product can no longer be sold.
A delisted product can still be sold but is not recommended for reorder.
entries.quote: A Deactivated product removes it from being sold. A Delisted product can still be sold but will not be recommended for reorder.

entries.title: Sell a product by weight without a scale barcode
steps: Set the product's price as the price per unit (per lb, per oz).
At the POS scan the item, key the weight, then press Change Quantity.
Example: 5 lb at $1.70/lb: scan, press 5, Change Quantity, and it rings $8.50.
entries.quote: Then at the POS, use the Change Quantity button to input the weight.

entries.title: "The Order Total Cannot be Exceeded When Using Payment Type: (XXXX)"
steps: The cashier entered more than the sale total for a payment method that does not allow change.
To allow it: in KORONA Studio go to Settings > Payment Methods, edit the payment method, tick 'change due' and save.
Run Retrieve Master Data on every register that uses that payment method.
entries.quote: This message displays when the cashier is trying to process a transaction using more than the total amount displayed on the point of sale terminal using the selected payment method.

entries.title: Receipt prices are cut off on the screen (tablet)
steps: The display font size is set too high.
Reduce the font size in the font size settings.
entries.quote: If you load KORONA POS on a tablet, the receipts prices may be cut off from the preview. This is because the display size of the fonts is set too high.

entries.title: How Korona rounds sales tax on a receipt
steps: Net amounts are added together and tax is applied to the sum, then rounded.
Items with different tax rates are grouped and rounded per tax rate.
entries.quote: The net amounts are added together on the receipt, and the tax is then applied to the sum

entries.title: Text disappears after saving in KORONA Studio (receipt header, footer, coupon text)
steps: Check your browser extensions.
There is a known issue with Grammarly; disable it for koronacloud.com.
entries.quote: There is a known issue with the popular extension Grammarly. Please disable it for koronacloud.com.

entries.title: Selling an item tax-free
steps: Taxes sit in Sectors; a cashier can switch sector at the POS to sell a product with its standard tax or tax-free.
Sectors and tax rates are set up in KORONA Studio under Settings.
entries.quote: You can switch between sectors at the POS so that you can sell a product with its standard tax or tax-free.

entries.title: Connect QuickBooks to Korona
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Data Exchange.
Type QuickBooks in the blank field at the top and press Add.
Select Quickbooks Online, click Add a New Connection, then Connect to Quickbooks and log in.
Add organizational units to the connection and choose a start date for syncing end of day statements.
entries.quote: At the top of the page in the blank field, type in QuickBooks, then press Add.

entries.title: Find a kitchen (network) printer's IP address
steps: Turn the printer off.
Hold down the feed button.
Turn the printer on while still holding the feed button.
A long status sheet prints; look for 'IP Address' or 'IPv4 Address'.
entries.quote: If this was done correctly, the printer should print a long status sheet. On there, look for “IP Address” or “IPv4 Address”.

entries.title: Add a kitchen printer to Korona
steps: Connect the printer to the network by Ethernet and note its IP address.
In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profiles and edit the profile used by the register that prints to it.
In Devices press Add; Type is Printer and Device is ESC/POS.
Change Port to Network and enter the IP address followed by :9100 in Default Value.
With several registers on one profile and several kitchen printers, a variable per register is needed; contact KORONA Support for help.
entries.quote: After adding the printer, change the “Port” to “Network”. Then, in the “Default Value” enter the IP address followed by :9100.

entries.title: Kitchen printer not bought from Korona will not work over the network
steps: A printer bought from Korona is already set up for Ethernet.
Otherwise the network option may need enabling on the printer; contact the printer manufacturer if you cannot enable it.
entries.quote: Please reach out to the printer manufacturer if you are unable to enable the printer to work over the network.

entries.title: An item is not printing on the kitchen ticket (or everything is)
steps: The kitchen printer only prints products that have the same Production Type as the printer.
In KORONA Studio check Settings > Production Types has a kitchen production type with Product Method set to Print.
Check that production type is added to the network printer in Settings > POS Profiles, Devices.
Add the production type to each product under Inventory > Products and Save.
Run Retrieve Master Data at the register.
entries.quote: Production Types are assigned to the printer and products, so the kitchen printer only prints products with the same production type.
entries.note: The Retrieve Master Data step comes from Korona's general rule that back-office changes must be retrieved at the POS.

entries.title: When the kitchen ticket prints
steps: The production type's trigger decides: 'after payment' prints once the customer has paid.
'after booking' prints when the cashier goes to the checkout page.
entries.quote: For the trigger, either use “after payment” for the kitchen ticket to print once the customer has paid, or “after booking” if you want it to print when the cashier goes to the checkout page.

entries.title: Which receipt printers work with Korona
steps: Most printers that support ESC/POS mode.
Paper must be 3 1/8 in / 80mm; mini 2 inch models are not supported.
Star MC series (for example MCP31LB) are not compatible.
Aclas all-in-one units with a built-in printer are not compatible.
entries.quote: We are not compatible with the Star MC series, e.g. “MCP31LB”, as they only support StarPRNT Emulation mode and not ESC/POS.

entries.title: Receipt paper size for Korona printers
steps: Use 3 1/8 inch (80mm) receipt paper.
entries.quote: The printer must use 3 1/8 in / 80mm receipt printer paper (no mini/2in models).

entries.title: Star printer not printing from Korona
steps: When the Star software is first run, set the printer to ESC/POS Mode; this has to be selected each time the Star software is launched.
Inside the software go to Print Job Routing and enable ESC/POS routing too.
entries.quote: Then, inside the software, go to Print Job Routing and enable ESC/POS routing there as well.

entries.title: Set up a receipt printer on a Windows register
steps: Download and install the driver for the printer's brand and model.
In Windows, Settings > Devices and Printers, right click the printer, open Properties and copy its name.
In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profile and edit the Windows POS Profile.
With one register, paste the name into Default Value for the printer (and cash drawer).
With two or more, create a 'printer' variable, then set its value per register under Sales > Points of Sale.
Restart the KORONA POS software and run a cash sale to test printer and drawer.
entries.quote: Reboot the KORONA POS software and then try a cash sale to test the printer and cash drawer.

entries.title: Epson printer set up with the TM Virtual Port Driver stopped working
steps: A recent Windows update broke the virtual port method.
Install the normal printer driver for the Epson model instead.
Then add the printer in Korona as a system printer, with the variable being the printer's name in Windows.
entries.quote: Note: A recent Windows update has broken this, we recommend installing the printer driver for your requisite Epson Printer from here.

entries.title: Add a cash drawer in Korona
steps: The cash drawer nearly always connects to the back of the receipt printer.
In the POS Profile click +Add Device and select Cash Drawer; the device is ESC/POS.
Fill in the remaining settings to match the printer it is attached to.
entries.quote: Fill out the rest of the settings according to the printer settings it is attached to. They should match each other.

entries.title: Add a receipt printer in Korona
steps: In the POS Profile click +Add Device and select Printer as Type.
Choose the device; Epson and ESC/POS are the most common.
Assign a Port: System Printer for printers installed in Windows, or USB_LPT1 for USB printers on Linux.
For a System Printer, set a variable under Port Parameter that holds the printer's name in Windows.
entries.quote: For Printers that are installed as System Printers, you’ll need to assign a Variable under the Port Parameter by referencing the printer’s name in Windows.

entries.title: Device Configuration Variables: one profile, different devices per register
steps: A Default Value applies to every register using the POS profile.
A Variable is set per register under Sales > Points of Sale, Device Configuration Variables.
This lets one profile serve several registers whose printers or card terminals have different names or IP addresses.
entries.quote: Default Value would be used for ALL devices using this POS profile, whereas a Variable can be configured per point of sale.

entries.title: How the barcode scanner works with Korona
steps: Most USB barcode scanners work as soon as they are plugged into the register.
The scanner acts like a keyboard: it types the code and presses Enter.
entries.quote: Most USB barcode scanners will work out of the box when plugged into your terminal running KORONA POS.

entries.title: Scanned number appears on screen but nothing happens
steps: The scanner is not sending a carriage return (the Enter key).
Enable it by scanning the set-up barcode from the scanner's quick-start guide.
entries.quote: When you scan a barcode, if you see that a number has been entered into the POS, but nothing else has happened, you will need to enable the scanner to send a “carriage return.”

entries.title: Scanned code has extra or missing digits, so the item is not found
steps: The scanner's 'leading numbers', 'check numbers' or 'country code' settings do not match how codes were entered in the catalog.
Change them by scanning the set-up barcodes from the scanner's guide.
If a 12-digit UPC-A scans with an extra 0 at the front, the country code is enabled.
Be consistent: store all product codes the same way and set the scanner to match.
entries.quote: When you scan a barcode, if numbers are added or subtracted to the end or beginning of the code, you will need to enable or disable “leading numbers,” “check numbers”, or possibly even the “country code.”

entries.title: Change a barcode scanner's settings
steps: Print the set-up barcodes from the scanner's quick-start guide.
Scan them with the scanner.
Korona links guides for the Honeywell Voyager 1400, Aures PS50 II, Motorola DS9208 and Welquic scanners.
entries.quote: In order to change the settings on your scanner, you need to print out the set-up barcodes and scan them with your barcode scanner.

entries.title: Scanner will not read QR codes or codes on a phone screen
steps: Only 2D scanners read QR codes and codes shown on screens; 1D scanners do not.
entries.quote: The most prominent difference is that 2D scanners are capable of reading QR codes as well as reading data off of other screens (such as smartphones or tablets).

entries.title: Add a barcode to a product with the scanner
steps: Attach the scanner to the computer where you use KORONA Studio.
On the product click Add New Code, scan the item, then Save.
Product numbers and codes must be unique and not attached to any other product.
entries.quote: With your scanner attached to the computer accessing the cloud, click Add New Code, scan the item, and then click Save.

entries.title: Set up the Korona all-in-one register and its accessories
steps: Slide the back cover off in the direction of the arrow (under the customer display, under 'Touch all-in-one').
Plug the Ethernet cable into the side of the terminal.
Plug the printer and scanner into the USB ports next to and below the Ethernet port; plug in the printer's power.
Plug the cash drawer into the phone-type jack on the printer.
Connect the card terminal with a different Ethernet cable to its own Ethernet outlet.
Refit the cover with the cords through the opening at the bottom, plug into power and press the power button.
At the Korona POS login screen, log on with code 1.
entries.quote: Both POS and Credit Card terminal should be plugged into their own separate Ethernet outlets.

entries.title: First login on a new Korona register
steps: Once the Korona POS Login Screen appears, log on with the code 1.
entries.quote: Once the Korona POS Login Screen appears, you can log on using the code 1 (one).

entries.title: Register will not complete any more transactions today (trial mode)
steps: In the test phase the register is limited to 30 transactions per day.
When the limit is reached the cashier is told and no more transactions can be completed that day.
The account has to be taken live to remove the limit.
entries.quote: Lastly, the number of transactions per day is limited in the test phase to 30 per day.

entries.title: Receipt says it is not for live use / message after every sale
steps: The account is still in the test phase.
A text on the receipt and a message after each transaction remind the cashier of this.
entries.quote: A text field appears on the receipt during the test phase, which indicates that the document is not intended for live use.

entries.title: Install the Korona POS software on a register
steps: Log in to KORONA Studio; first time, use the password from the account activation email.
On the dashboard click Configure POS (or go to Sales > Points of Sale).
Under Authentication click Download Terminal Software and pick the operating system.
Run the downloaded file; a window asks for an installation token.
In KORONA Studio, on the edit point of sale page, click Generate Installation Token, copy the code and paste it into the window.
entries.quote: To get the install token, go back to the KORONA Studio edit point of sale page and select the button “Generate Installation Token” above the “Download Terminal Software” button.

entries.title: Couple the register to the account
steps: Log in on the register with the same email and password as KORONA Studio.
Select the POS being set up (picked automatically if there is only one).
The POS restarts; the first start after coupling usually takes several minutes.
entries.quote: The first start after coupling the POS will usually take several minutes, but future POS starts will be significantly faster.

entries.title: Do not know the cashier login code on a new account
steps: Try 1, the default login code for new accounts.
Cashier logins are changed and added in KORONA Studio under Employees > Cashiers.
entries.quote: If you do not know your login code, try “1”. This is the default login code for new accounts.

entries.title: Browser warns when downloading the Korona client
steps: Open the drop-down on the warning and select Keep to continue the download.
entries.quote: Go to the drop-down and select "Keep" to continue the download.

entries.title: Take a Korona account from demo mode to live
steps: Run an end of day on every register first.
Log in to KORONA Studio; 'Demo Mode' with a cloud icon shows at the top left if still in demo.
Set up the subscription; the button then changes to Start Live Mode.
Click Start Live Mode and choose which trial data to delete.
Press 'Start Live Mode Now!' and complete the captcha.
entries.quote: Don’t forget to to do an End of Day on the POS before completing this step.

entries.title: Going live can only be done once
steps: Live mode can only be activated once.
Data marked for removal cannot be recovered.
Products, commodity groups, cashiers, users and settings are kept.
entries.quote: Live mode can only be activated once.  Data that was marked for removal can not be recovered.

entries.title: Reset the KORONA Studio password step by step
steps: On the KORONA login screen click the forgot password link below the password box.
Enter your email address and confirm.
Open the email, follow the link and click generate a new password; you get a temporary password.
Log in, click your name at the upper right, then My User Account.
Click Change Password, enter the temporary password and the new one, confirm, and press Change Password.
entries.quote: Now go and check your email for the link to reset your password and click generate a new password. You will be provided with a temporary password to login to your account.

entries.title: Changing the login email needs approval
steps: After you click Request Change, a ticket goes to KORONA Support for review.
You get an email confirmation once it is approved.
entries.quote: Once you click Request Change, a ticket will be generated for our KORONA Support team to review.

entries.title: When the register picks up back-office changes on its own
steps: The register downloads KORONA Studio changes at every restart and after each end-of-day statement.
So it usually refreshes at least once a day.
For an immediate update use Retrieve Master Data, by default under function tab 3.
entries.quote: The point of sale will automatically download KORONA Studio back office changes with every restart and after generating an end-of-day statement.

entries.title: Change to a printer, drawer, card terminal or POS profile is not taking effect
steps: Run Retrieve Master Data at the register.
Then restart the POS software; changes to peripherals, payment terminals or services, and POS profiles need a restart.
If button changes do not show after Retrieve Master Data, restart the POS software too.
entries.quote: Usually, button changes do not require a POS restart. However, if button changes are not applied after you retrieve master data, try restarting the POS software.

entries.title: Receipt prices cut off on a tablet screen: reduce the Windows font scaling
steps: Exit KORONA POS to the Windows desktop (in standalone mode, swipe from the left edge, tap an empty space, and close KORONA POS from Task Manager).
Long-press the desktop and choose Display Settings.
Find the font size option; most tablets are at 150%. Set it to 100%.
Apply, sign out of Windows and sign back in.
Restart KORONA POS and log in.
entries.quote: Most tablets will be set to 150% by default. Under Windows 10, drag the slider down to 100%.

entries.title: Genius terminal: find its IP address
steps: Connect the Genius to its power adapter and an Ethernet cable.
When it has booted, press the 0 button three times.
Enter the administrator password and note the IP address.
entries.quote: When it finishes booting up, press the 0 button three times.

entries.title: Connect a Genius (Cayan) terminal to Korona
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profile, open the profile, Devices, Add Devices.
Set Type to Credit Terminal and Device to Genius Credit Terminal; set Port to Network.
Enter the terminal's IP address as the Port Parameter default value or a variable.
In settings enter the SiteId, MerchantKey and MerchantName from Cayan exactly.
Create a payment method with Payment Service 'Credit Terminal' and add a payment button.
At the register run Retrieve Master Data, then restart the POS software.
entries.quote: NOTE* This information MUST be exact, or the terminal will NOT work.

entries.title: Genius: cannot process returns or refunds to card
steps: The payment method needs the 'Change Due?' checkbox ticked in KORONA Studio under Settings > Payment Methods.
entries.quote: If you wish to be able to process returns or refunds, you will also need to tick the “Change Due?” checkbox.

entries.title: Genius: tip prompt on the terminal
steps: Put 'tip' in the payment method's service parameter.
Cayan must also enable the tip prompt for it to appear on the Genius.
entries.quote: Cayan must enable this functionality for the tip prompt to appear on the Genius.

entries.title: Activate a new BlockChyp terminal
steps: Plug the terminal into Ethernet and power.
Log in to the BlockChyp back end, open the merchant account and select Activate Terminal under Active Terminals.
Boot the terminal; enter the code it shows into the Activation Code field.
Name the device (Korona suggests the same name as the POS it connects to).
Click Activate Terminal; the terminal screen flashes 'Now Activated'.
entries.quote: Once you hit Activate Terminal the screen on the terminal should change and flash “Now Activated”.

entries.title: Connect a BlockChyp terminal to Korona
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profiles and add BlockChyp as the Credit Terminal.
Add the settings apiKey, bearerToken, signingKey, terminalName, useLineItemDisplay and signatureCapture, exactly spelled and capitalized.
Generate the credentials in BlockChyp under Merchant Tools > API Credentials; they display only once.
Retrieve master data at the POS, restart the POS, restart the BlockChyp terminal, and run a test transaction.
entries.quote: From there you should be good to retrieve master data at your POS, restart the POS, restart the BlockChyp terminal, and then make a test transaction to ensure everything is correctly configured.

entries.title: BlockChyp cash discounting needs POS version 2.1.23 or above
steps: Check the POS version in KORONA Studio under Sales > Points of Sale.
If it is below 2.1.23, contact support to update.
entries.quote: It will have to be set to 2.1.23 or above in order for the remaining steps to work. If you are below this version, please contact support and we can help with updating.

entries.title: Connect an Econduit card terminal to Korona
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profile and +Add Device: Credit Terminal, Econduit Credit Terminal.
Set the Port to Network.
Fill in the Settings with the details from your merchant account.
Retrieve master data and restart the point of sale.
entries.quote: Whenever you change any setting under the POS profile, you must retrieve the master data and restart your point of sale for the changes to occur.

entries.title: Sell a gift card
steps: Press the Gift Card button.
Scan the card's barcode (or enter its serial number) and press Apply.
Enter the dollar amount to load and press Enter.
Press Total and take payment as usual.
entries.quote: We begin by adding our gift card to the receipt by pressing the Gift Card button. The screen will ask you for a serial number.

entries.title: Take payment with a gift card
steps: Press Total to go to the payment screen.
Select Gift Card and enter the amount the customer wants to use.
Scan the card; the number can also be typed in and confirmed with Enter.
If a balance remains on the sale, the payment screen returns for another payment.
entries.quote: The cashier now scans the card (it says scan or swipe, but you can also manually type in a number and press enter).

entries.title: Check a gift card balance
steps: At the register select Check Prepaid Card on the main screen and scan the card; the balance is shown.
In KORONA Studio, Sales > Prepaid cards lists every card with its current value.
entries.quote: On the main screen, select “Check Prepaid Card.” Since we are using preprinted cards, we will scan the barcode on that card.

entries.title: Gift cards are set up by default on new Korona accounts
steps: New accounts come with gift cards, the gift card payment method and its buttons already set up.
If they are missing, use the Gift Card Assistant in the Getting Started widget on the KORONA Studio dashboard.
entries.quote: New KORONA POS accounts come with gift cards, the gift card payment method, and the related buttons already set up by default.

entries.title: New gift card button or payment method is not on the register
steps: Run Retrieve Master Data on the register.
Restart the POS software.
entries.quote: Remember to Retrieve Master Data and restart the POS Software to add the payment method and the button to the terminal.

entries.title: Create a gift card from the back office
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Sales > Prepaid Cards and click New.
Enter the amount, a comment and the card number, and click Create.
The card can then be used at the POS.
entries.quote: Click New, enter the Amount, Comment, and Card Number, and click Create. This gift card may now be used at the POS.

entries.title: Age verification has to be enabled by KORONA support
steps: Age verification is not on by default; KORONA POS Technical Support enables and sets it up, including files on the register.
Each age-restricted product must be in a tax Sector with 21+ (or 18+) in its name.
entries.quote: If you need Age Verification for your POS system, you must contact KORONA POS Technical Support so they can enable and set it up for you.

entries.title: Answer the age verification prompt
steps: When an age-restricted item is on the receipt, the prompt appears after pressing Total.
Type the customer's birth date on the keypad.
With a 2D driver's-license scanner, scan the back of the licence to fill it in.
If the date meets the minimum age, carry on with payment.
entries.quote: The cashier can type in the birth date using the keypad, as seen above, or, if you have specific 2D Driver’s License Barcode Scanners, you can scan the back of the driver’s license to auto-populate the birth date.

entries.title: Cannot take payment after skipping the age verification screen
steps: Pressing Back reaches the payment screen, but the payment cannot be finalized.
Go back and enter a valid birth date, or remove the age-restricted item from the receipt.
entries.quote: The only way to finalize this payment would be to go back and remove the age-restricted item from the receipt or type in a valid birth date.

entries.title: A product does not trigger the age prompt
steps: In KORONA Studio assign the 21+ tax Sector to that product (products can be mass-edited).
Every product that should trigger the check must be in the 21+ sector.
entries.quote: You’ll want to ensure you assign all products that need to trigger the age verification to the 21+ sector.

entries.title: EBT payments need their own payment method setting
steps: An EBT payment method must include the service parameter ebtfood or ebtcash in KORONA Studio under Settings > Payment Methods.
entries.quote: EBT transactions require that the payment method include the service parameter ebtfood or ebtcash

entries.title: Cash drawer does not open (or opens) for a particular payment type
steps: Each payment method has a Use Cash Drawer option; when on, the drawer opens when the payment completes.
Change it in KORONA Studio under Settings > Payment Methods, then retrieve master data.
entries.quote: If activated, the cash drawer will open upon payment completion
entries.note: The retrieve-master-data step comes from Korona's general rule for back-office changes.

entries.title: Print an extra receipt copy for card payments
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Payment Methods and edit the payment method.
Set Receipt Print Copies to the number of additional copies wanted and Save.
entries.quote: How many additional copies of the receipt are printed after payment has been processed by the point of sale

entries.title: A payment method insists on a customer number
steps: The payment method has Force Customer Number switched on, so the receipt must have a customer set.
entries.quote: When activated, receipts made on this payment method must have a customer number set.

entries.title: Add a payment method button to the register
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Button Configurations, select the configuration and click the layouts button.
Open the layout, right-click an empty square and choose Select Payment Method.
Pick the payment method, click Add, and Save.
entries.quote: Right-click on that square and click “Select Payment Method” from the context menu.

entries.title: Open a card tab (take a pre-authorization)
steps: Ring the items and go to the payment screen.
Press the Credit Pre-Auth button, enter the amount and press Enter.
The card is run on the card terminal.
Two tip slips print along with the itemized receipt.
entries.quote: Proceed to the payment screen and select the Credit Pre-Auth button that was created earlier. Add the amount you wish to charge and hit Enter.
entries.note: Not all processors and card terminals support pre-auth/post-auth; Korona calls Tip Adjustment the newer method.

entries.title: Close a pre-auth receipt and add the tip
steps: Open the receipt archive; Show Open Pre-Authorizations filters to receipts waiting to be closed.
Select the receipt and press Re-Open Receipt.
Enter the tip amount and press Apply Payment Tip; enter 0 if there is no tip.
Press Enter to finalize; the card is charged the final amount.
entries.quote: If the customer did not leave a tip, you must still enter “0” to close out the receipt.

entries.title: Pre-auth tabs must be closed before end of day
steps: A pre-auth receipt stays open until it is finalized at the register.
If it is still open when End of Day runs, it is not approved and the card is not charged.
Close every open pre-auth receipt before running end of day.
entries.quote: If an open receipt is not closed when the End of Day runs, it will not be approved, nor will the card be charged for any payment.

entries.title: Apply Payment Tip asks for a payment method first
steps: A tip can only be applied after a payment is on the receipt.
Run the Credit Pre-Auth first, then reopen the receipt to apply the tip.
entries.quote: However, selecting that button now will create a pop-up asking for a payment method to be applied first.

entries.title: Pre-auth/post-auth is not supported by every processor
steps: Not all processors and card terminals support pre-auth and post-auth.
The newer method is Tip Adjustment.
Ask the processor which they support.
entries.quote: Not all processors and credit terminals support pre-auth and post-auth functions. The newer method is Tip Adjustment.

entries.title: Redeem a voucher
steps: For single- and multi-purpose vouchers press Redeem Voucher and enter or scan the voucher number.
Deposit vouchers are redeemed by scanning their barcode.
After scanning a deposit voucher, keep the deposit receipt, or it can be redeemed again.
entries.quote: THE CASHIER MUST COLLECT THE DEPOSIT RECEIPT AFTER SCANNING OR IT CAN BE REDEEMED AGAIN.

entries.title: Cancel a voucher
steps: Vouchers do not show as items on a receipt.
Press the Cancel Voucher button, then enter or scan the voucher.
entries.quote: Vouchers are not shown as items on a receipt. Therefore in order to cancel a voucher, a button with the function ‘Cancel Voucher’ would need to be used.

entries.title: Check a voucher's status
steps: Press the Show Voucher button, then enter or scan the voucher.
entries.quote: To see the status of a voucher the ‘Show Voucher’ function would need to be used.

entries.title: Vouchers are an add-on package
steps: Vouchers must be added to the KORONA Studio account as a package; contact support to add it.
entries.quote: Vouchers is an additional package that can be added to your KORONA Studio account.

entries.title: Set up the customer-facing display
steps: On Windows the display must show up as a secondary monitor in Windows settings.
In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Customer Displays, create one, and for Display usually choose 'On Display 2'.
Choose what shows on the Welcome, Booking and Closed screens and Save.
In Sales > Points of Sale edit the POS and pick the display under Customer Display.
Restart the POS.
entries.quote: For Windows POS hardware setups, the display needs to show up as a secondary monitor in the Windows settings.

entries.title: Customer display changes are not showing
steps: For a newly assigned display, restart the POS.
If the display already existed and only settings changed, run Retrieve Master Data.
entries.quote: If the display already existed and you only changed the settings, retrieve master data to update it.

entries.title: Stop cash drops and deposits showing on the customer display
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Accounts.
Untick 'Show transaction on customer display' for that account.
entries.quote: Go to Settings > Accounts and uncheck the box for “Show transaction on customer display”.

entries.title: Fit a customer display to a Partner Tech A5 II register
steps: Power off the POS and remove the power cable and all other cables first.
You need a flathead and a Phillips screwdriver and a flat surface; lay a towel under the screen.
Follow Korona's installation video.
Then set the display up in KORONA Studio.
entries.quote: IMPORTANT: Power off the POS and remove the power cable before installing the customer display.

entries.title: Set up a PartnerTech SP-5514 register
steps: Remove the screws on the back with a Phillips screwdriver and pull off the cover.
Plug the network cable into the LAN slot.
Plug the printer into a USB slot (to the right of the LAN slot) and into power.
Plug the cash drawer into the phone-type jack on the printer.
Refit the covers, plug into power and press the power button.
At the KORONA POS login screen log on with code 1.
entries.quote: Using a Phillips head screwdriver, remove the screws on the back of the POS and pull off the cover.

entries.title: Set up a PartnerTech A5 register
steps: Lift the protective covers and remove both screws holding the back plate; slide the plate off.
Plug the network cable into LAN 1 or LAN 2.
Plug the printer into a USB slot (to the right of the LAN slots) and into power.
Plug the cash drawer into the phone-type jack on the printer.
Plug in power and press the power button.
At the KORONA POS login screen log on with code 1.
entries.quote: You can use either of the marked LAN ports “LAN 1” or “LAN 2.”

entries.title: Set up an Aures Sango register
steps: Press the button on the back of the side cover and remove the cover at an angle.
Plug the network cable into the LAN slot below the blue USB 3.0 ports.
Plug the printer into the USB slot below the LAN slots and into power.
Plug the cash drawer into the phone-type jack on the printer.
Refit the covers, plug into power and press the power button.
At the KORONA POS login screen log on with code 1.
entries.quote: Press the button on the back of the side cover to release the cover and gently remove it at an angle.

entries.title: Support hours printed on Korona hardware setup guides
steps: The Aures Sango and SP-5514 setup guides give Mon-Fri 9:00AM to 6:00PM Pacific on +1 (702)-997-7672.
entries.quote: Mon-Fri 9:00AM to 6:00PM Pacific Time
entries.note: Disagrees with Korona's Contact Us page, which says general support is Monday to Friday 6 AM to 6 PM PT with 24/7 emergency support.

entries.title: Log in to the handheld inventory app (Korona.mde)
steps: Install 'Korona.mde' from the Google Play Store; uninstall any old version first.
The first time, log in with your KORONA Studio credentials.
After that, employees log in with their cashier login code and choose the store location.
entries.quote: Once the app is downloaded and installed, find it in your applications and login with your KORONA Studio credentials for the first time. Going forward, employees will log in using their Cashier login code.

entries.title: Count inventory with the handheld app
steps: Retrieve master data in the app before starting.
Open Inventories and tap + to create a count, or open an existing one.
Tap the magnifying glass to find a product, or scan it.
Key the quantity and press plus to add, or equals to set the count; scanning again adds 1 each time.
When done, swipe left on the inventory in the list and press upload.
entries.quote: To upload your changes to the cloud from the inventory lists screen, swipe left on the inventory and press ‘upload.’

entries.title: Handheld app: retrieve master data before, upload after
steps: Always retrieve master data before working on an inventory count.
Press Upload when finished.
entries.quote: Always manually retrieve master data BEFORE working on an Inventory Count and hit Upload after working on one

entries.title: Handheld app: refresh stock values
steps: Swipe down from the top of the screen.
entries.quote: Swipe down from the top of the screen to refresh stock values.

entries.title: Receive stock with the handheld app
steps: Open Stock Receipts and press +; start from a stock order, a dispatch notification, or an empty receipt.
Search for or scan the items; plus adds, equals sets the amount, scanning again adds 1.
Swipe left on the stock receipt to upload it.
Stock receipts must then be booked from the back office.
entries.quote: Stock receipts have to be booked from the backend.

entries.title: Handheld app does not show prices in Product Information
steps: Tap the menu icon at the top left, then Settings.
Scroll to the Product Information tab and enable retail and/or purchase prices.
entries.quote: The retail and purchase prices for products are not shown by default but can be added in the KORONA MDE settings.

entries.title: A product rings up at the wrong price
steps: In KORONA Studio open the product and check the Prices section; each column is a Price Group.
Check which Price Group is set for the Customer Group and the Organizational Unit (Settings > Customer Groups / Organizational Units).
Check whether a customer or a button at the POS is applying a different Customer Group.
Check Store Prices (button at the top of the product); a store price overrides any price group price.
After correcting, retrieve master data at the register.
entries.quote: Store Prices will override any price set by a Price Group.
entries.note: The retrieve-master-data step comes from Korona's general rule for back-office changes.

entries.title: Price changed when a customer was added to the sale
steps: A Customer Group with a different Price Group overrides the product's current price.
Setting a customer by number does not automatically apply their Customer Group.
entries.quote: Applying a Customer Group with a different Price Group will override the current price for the product and apply the price from the newly applied Customer Group.

entries.title: Inventory count is wrong
steps: Check whether inventory tracking was ever disabled; that resets the count.
Check sales are syncing; a register not connected to the internet syncs late and throws counts off.
Check all stock receipts and inventory counts are booked.
Check the register is assigned to the right warehouse (Sales tab, point of sale screen).
Look at Evaluations > Stock History Report for the product.
entries.quote: If inventory tracking is EVER disabled, it will reset the inventory count.

entries.title: Sales reach the back office late when the register is offline
steps: Sales sync late if the POS is not connected to the internet.
Doing an inventory count while the POS has not synced throws the count off.
entries.quote: Sales can also sync late if the POS is not connected to the internet.

entries.title: Promotion is not triggering on a product
steps: In KORONA Studio open the product under Inventory > Products and make sure Is Discountable is ticked and saved.
At the register go to the Total screen; discounts only apply there.
Check the promotion's tag, date and customer group.
entries.quote: Ensure you’ve gone to the Total Screen on the POS. Discounts only apply after going to the Total Screen.

entries.title: Find the card's last 4 digits and approval for a past sale
steps: Open the Receipt Archive at the POS, type the receipt number and press Enter.
At the bottom, 'Account: xxxx' is the last 4 of the card and 'Approval' is the transaction token.
Without the receipt number: in KORONA Studio go to Sales > Receipts, filter by Payment Method = Credit, date and gross total.
entries.quote: At the bottom, it will show you “Account: xxxx“, which is the last 4 of the card number. “Approval” is the Transaction Token.

entries.title: Chargebacks and signatures
steps: Korona notes the major card brands no longer require a signature for purchases, so one is not typically needed to dispute a chargeback.
entries.quote: thus a signature is not typically required to dispute a charge back

entries.title: Sell an item that is not in the catalog (open product)
steps: In KORONA Studio create a product with name, commodity group, assortment and sector, leaving prices blank.
Set it to Price changeable and save.
Click To Button, choose Quick Keys and place the button.
Run Retrieve Master Data at the register.
entries.quote: Open products are used if you need to quickly sell either a new product or a product you don’t want to enter into KORONA Studio.

entries.title: Discount Reasons report: what (PR), (P) and (RD) mean
steps: (PR): a price rule caused the discount.
(P): a promotion caused it.
(RD): a receipt discount triggered manually at the POS.
entries.quote: (RD) – This indicates a Receipt Discount was triggered manually at the POS via a button or external system call.

entries.title: Emailed (digital) receipts are not arriving
steps: In KORONA Studio click your username at the top left and open My Company Data.
Make sure Email Alias is not blank.
entries.quote: Ensure the section labeled “Email Alias” is not left blank.

entries.title: Turn on digital receipts
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profile, and in the Receipt field choose Digital Receipt and save.
Retrieve master data and restart the point of sale.
The customer display then shows a QR code; the customer scans it and enters their email.
entries.quote: Start by navigating to Settings > POS Profile. There is a field called Receipt with multiple options to choose from. Click Digital Receipt and save.

entries.title: Email a receipt by typing the customer's address
steps: Type the email address with the on-screen keyboard.
Press Enter (if set up with number ranges) or the 'Set email for digital receipt dispatch' button.
A popup confirms a digital receipt will be sent.
entries.quote: It will give you a popup notifying you that a digital receipt will be sent.

entries.title: Add a cashier or change a login code
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Employees > Cashiers.
Click +New, or select a cashier and press Edit.
Fill in a unique cashier number, first and last name, a Login Code and a Cashier Role.
Press Save.
entries.quote: Another required field is the Login Code for the point of sale.

entries.title: Sample cashiers on a new Korona account
steps: The system ships with two sample cashiers, John Doe and Jane Doe, with login codes 1 and 2.
Change or remove them once real cashiers are set up.
entries.quote: By default, the system comes with 2 sample cashiers configured – John Doe and Jane Doe – with login codes “1” and “2,” respectively.
entries.note: Advice to change or remove them is ours, not the source's.

entries.title: Stop a cashier's full name printing on receipts
steps: In KORONA Studio fill in the cashier's alias field; the receipt shows the alias instead of the full name.
entries.quote: If you do not want the cashier’s full name printed on the receipt, fill out the alias field in the back office.

entries.title: Block a cashier who has left
steps: Deleting a cashier cannot be reversed.
If work times are still needed for payroll, change the login code or use the Lock option instead of deleting.
entries.quote: we recommend changing the employees’ login codes to restrict access or locking the cashier using the Lock option before deleting the cashier record

entries.title: "You are not authorized to perform this action."
steps: The cashier's role lacks the permission for that action.
Have someone with the permission do it, or change the role in KORONA Studio under Employees > Cashier Roles.
Move the permission from the left box to the right and save.
entries.quote: they will get a pop up notification stating “You are not authorized to perform this action.”

entries.title: Korona cashier permissions: what each allows
steps: Cancel Items: remove line items.
Cancel Receipt: cancel an unfinished receipt.
Return: process returns, void receipts, and ring negative quantities.
Void Receipt: void finalized receipts.
Price: override item prices even when the product does not allow it.
Open Cash Drawer: use the Open Cash Drawer button.
Reports: pull POS reports.
Foreign Receipt: open receipts assigned to other cashiers.
Blank Receipt: finalize a receipt with no items.
entries.quote: Allows the cashier to process item returns, void receipts, and place negative quantities of products on the receipt.

entries.title: Cashier cannot remove the last item from a receipt
steps: Without the Cancel Last Receipt Item permission a cashier cannot remove the last item.
Use Cancel Receipt, or have the role changed in KORONA Studio.
entries.quote: Without this permission, cashiers are not allowed to remove the last item from the receipt.
entries.note: The Cancel Receipt suggestion needs the Cancel Receipt permission.

entries.title: Void Item button
steps: Voids a single item from the receipt.
entries.quote: Void Item: Voids a single item from a receipt.

entries.title: Immediate Cancellation button
steps: Removes the most recent item added to the receipt, but nothing before it.
entries.quote: will allow the removal of the most recent item added to the receipt, but nothing prior to that

entries.title: Cash Void button: undo a cash payment before the receipt is finished
steps: Cancels a cash payment taken at the POS before the receipt is finalized.
It only works from the payment layout.
entries.quote: Cash Void: Cancels any cash payment taken at the POS before the finalization of the receipt. This function only works from the payment layout.

entries.title: Return Item button: return one item inside a normal sale
steps: Marks a product on a normal transaction as a return of goods and asks for a return reason.
Useful for exchanges, since the whole receipt is not turned into a return.
entries.quote: Return Item: Sets a product on a normal transaction to be a “Return of Goods” and prompts you to enter a return reason.

entries.title: Return page button
steps: Search for a receipt number and refund individual items on it without going to the receipt archive.
entries.quote: Return page: Allows you to search for a receipt number and refund individual items on that receipt without going to the receipt archive.

entries.title: Receipt Reversal button
steps: Reverses a receipt as if the transaction did not happen; similar to Void Receipt.
entries.quote: Receipt Reversal: Reverses a receipt, treating it as if the transaction did not happen. Similar to Void Receipt.

entries.title: Receipt Print button reprints the second most recent receipt
steps: Receipt Print reprints the 2nd most recent (not the last) receipt in the print queue.
To reprint a specific receipt, use Print from the receipt archive.
entries.quote: Receipt Print: Reprints the 2nd most recent (not last) receipt in the print queue.
entries.note: The second step is from Korona's Print function page.

entries.title: Print reports at the register
steps: Print POS Report prints the activity of one POS for the day.
Print Cashier Report prints one cashier's sales for the period.
Print POS Week Report and Print POS Month Report print the previous week or month.
entries.quote: Print POS Report: Prints the activity of one POS for that day.

entries.title: Print POS Week Report for the current week
steps: The week report prints the previous week.
For the current week, enter a negative number to reflect days.
entries.quote: To print one for the current week, you must enter a negative number to reflect days.

entries.title: Cash Check
steps: Checks whether the money in the drawer matches what the POS expects.
It only works on the balance screen.
entries.quote: Is used as a way to check if the amount of money that’s inside the cash drawer is the expected amount according to the POS.

entries.title: Change Item Price button
steps: Adjusts the dollar amount on a product.
entries.quote: Change Item Price: Allows for the $ amount on a product to be adjusted.

entries.title: Add Discount and Item Discount buttons
steps: Add Discount adds a % discount to the highlighted product, on top of any existing discounts.
Item Discount applies a % discount to the highlighted item(s).
entries.quote: Add Discount: Adds a % discount to the highlighted product on the receipt. This applies on top of any other existing discounts.

entries.title: Target Price Discount button
steps: Applies the price you want to a product and shows the discount as a percentage.
entries.quote: Target Price Discount: Applies the price you desire to a product and reflects the discount in a percentage.

entries.title: Tax-free sale (for example EBT): Apply Alternative Sector
steps: Apply Alternative Sector changes the selected products to their alternative tax sector, for example for a tax-free EBT sale.
Apply Default Sector changes them back.
entries.quote: Apply Alternative Sector and Apply Default Sector: Changes the selected products to their alternative sector, e.g. for a tax-free EBT sale.

entries.title: Toggle Sector button must be pressed after all items are added
steps: Toggle Sector switches between tax sectors.
Press it after all items have been added.
entries.quote: Note* this button must be pressed after all items have been added.

entries.title: Clear a wrong entry
steps: Clear Input Line clears anything keyed by mistake before a function is chosen.
Backspace removes the last entry.
entries.quote: Clear Input Line: Helps clear any data from buttons pressed by mistake before selecting the intended function.

entries.title: Show or hide the on-screen keyboard
steps: The Keyboard function turns the virtual keyboard on or off.
entries.quote: Keyboard: Activates/deactivates the virtual keyboard on the screen.

entries.title: Price check
steps: Price Info looks up a product's price by product number and lets you select the product.
entries.quote: Is a price query function that allows you to look up the prices of products by searching for the product number.

entries.title: Check stock of a product from the register
steps: List Stocks shows a product's stock across warehouses, quantities on order and the last stock order.
entries.quote: List Stocks: Lists the stock of a product within multiple warehouses, the number of goods, the number of Ordered Goods, and the last known Stock Order.

entries.title: Find a customer at the register
steps: Customer Lookup searches customers by name, number or address.
entries.quote: Customer Lookup: Searches for Customers by name, number or address.

entries.title: Remove all coupons from a receipt
steps: Removes every coupon applied to the current receipt without cancelling the receipt.
entries.quote: Will allow you to remove all coupons applied to the current receipt instead of having to cancel the receipt.

entries.title: Receipt cannot be finalized: receipt finalization lock
steps: A receipt lock stops a receipt being finalized, for example until someone with more authority reviews it.
Remove Receipt Finalization Lock removes the lock from the current receipt.
entries.quote: Set receipt finalization lock: Locks the receipt, preventing it from being finalized.

entries.title: Restart POS and Exit Application buttons
steps: Restart POS restarts the point of sale terminal.
Exit Application closes the KORONA client immediately.
entries.quote: Exit Application: Exits out of the KORONA client application immediately.

entries.title: Revision: a manager steps in without losing the sale
steps: Revision switches login quickly without deleting the current ticket, so a manager can use a function the cashier is not allowed to.
entries.quote: Allows for a quick change of login at the POS without deleting the current ticket.

entries.title: Stop one item printing to the kitchen or ticket printer
steps: Select the item and press Deactivate Print by Production Type; that product will not trigger its print.
entries.quote: Deactivate Print by Production Type: Disables a product with a production type from triggering that production type.

entries.title: Send the kitchen print or activate a gift card manually
steps: Trigger Production manually triggers production types such as gift card activation, kitchen print or ticket activation.
entries.quote: Trigger Production: Manually triggers certain production types like gift card activation, kitchen print, or ticket activation.

entries.title: Clock in and out
steps: The Time Tracking function lets employees clock in and out, and for lunch breaks.
entries.quote: Time Tracking:  Allows employees to clock in and out of work as well as for lunch breaks.

entries.title: Tip as a percentage of the receipt
steps: Set % of Receipt Total adds a tip based on a percentage of the receipt total; several buttons can be set with different percentages.
entries.quote: Set % of Receipt Total: This function allows you to add a tip based on a percentage of the total receipt.

entries.title: Credit Card Terminal: Configuration (DataCap terminals)
steps: Updates DataCap card terminals.
Required if the processor's settings or file build are changed.
entries.quote: Credit Card Terminal: Configuration: Updates DataCap credit card terminals. If any settings from the Processor or File Build are changed, this is required.

entries.title: EBT balance check (DataCap terminals)
steps: Credit Card Terminal: EBT Balance Cash/Foodstamp shows EBT balances on DataCap card terminals.
entries.quote: Credit Card Terminal: EBT Balance Cash/Foodstamp: Used to show EBT balances for DataCap credit card terminals.

entries.title: ZVT card terminal functions do not apply in the US
steps: Diagnosis, Initializing, Maintenance and Repeat receipt apply only to ZVT card terminals used in the EU.
entries.quote: Only applies to ZVT credit card terminals that are used in the EU.

entries.title: Serial (RS-232) barcode scanner
steps: Activate Barcode Scanner enables RS-232 communication for serial-connected scanners.
entries.quote: Activate Barcode Scanner: For usage with Serial Connected Scanners, enables RS-232 communications.

entries.title: Handheld Manager
steps: Lists devices connected to KORONA, lets you accept or remove a device, and release receipts from a device.
entries.quote: Handheld Manager: Lists all devices connected to KORONA and allows the acceptance or removal of that device.

entries.title: Payment button: pay in the default method without the total screen
steps: Enter the amount paid in the input field and press Payment.
Change is displayed as normal.
entries.quote: You can enter the amount being paid in the item input field and then press the “payment” button to process that amount in the default method.

entries.title: Round Receipt Total Down
steps: Rounds the receipt total down by the amount entered; repeat to reverse.
Works only on the payment layout.
entries.quote: Round Receipt Total Down: Rounds the receipt total down by whatever amount you put in.

entries.title: Cancelled transactions are not in the receipt archive
steps: Show Receipt Archive lists the most recent receipts but not cancelled transactions.
entries.quote: Displays a list of the most recent receipts. It will not display canceled transactions.

entries.title: A button asks for a manager's or second cashier's login code
steps: Buttons can be restricted by role or set to need approval.
The action is blocked until a higher-level employee (or, in the alternative setup, a second user) enters their login code.
It is set in KORONA Studio under Settings > Button Configurations, on the button itself.
entries.quote: If they attempt a restricted action like a void, the system will block it until a higher-level employee uses their login code and approves the action.

entries.title: Park a sale under a name or order number and recall it later
steps: Ring the items.
Press Set Order Number and enter a number or name.
Press Park Receipt; this receipt will not pop back up by itself.
To recall it press Open Receipt via Order Number and select it from the list or enter the order number.
entries.quote: By pressing the button for Open Receipt via Order Number, the POS will take you to a list of all Park Receipts.

entries.title: A blank receipt opened when recalling an order number
steps: If the order number entered does not exist, the POS creates a new receipt with that number.
Check the number, or pick the receipt from the list instead.
entries.quote: If the entered order number does not exist, the POS will create a new receipt with the entered order number.

entries.title: Move items from one parked receipt to another
steps: Both receipts need an order number and must be parked.
Open the receipt you are moving items from with Open Receipt via Order Number.
Enter the order number of the receipt to move to in the panel at the bottom left.
Select the items to move.
Press Transfer Items.
entries.quote: Identify the receipt you wish to transfer items to by inputting its order number into the panel in the bottom left.

entries.title: Take a payment toward a store (house) account
steps: Add the account to the receipt.
Type the amount with a minus sign in front.
Process the transaction normally.
